text: EX-10.1 2 ea031260401ex10-1.htm TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER AGREEMENT, DATED NOVEMBER 17, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN HUBEI TAIHE BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. AND HARBIN AIKESAILUN BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD Exhibit 10.1 TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER AGREEMENT Date of Execution: November 17, 2026 Term of the Agreement: November 2026 to November 2031 Place of Execution: Beijing, China Transferee (Party A): Hubei Taihe Biotechnology Co., Ltd. Address: 7 th Floor, Building 4, Fanhai International SOHO City, Jianghan District, Wuhan, Hubei Province, PRC Transferor (Party B): Harbin Aikesailun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. Address: 5 th Floor, Unit 1, No. 5 Taihu North Street, Chuangye Building, Yingbin Road Concentrated Area, Harbin High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, Harbin, Heilongjiang, PRC RECITALS: Whereas, Party B agrees to transfer to Party A the technology and related rights and interests (the scope of which is set forth below) relating to the product “Aikesailun”-Branded Bovine Colostrum, Vitamin C and Lactoferrin Chewable Tablets; Whereas, the Health Food Registration No. is G20190038, and stated health functions to enhance immune function; Whereas, Party B represents it is the owner and agrees to transfer the formula to Party A, Whereas, Party A agrees to accept such transfer and pay the applicable transfer consideration. After arm’s-length consultation and based on their respective genuine intentions, the parties enter into this Technology Transfer Agreement. Article 1. Subject Matter of the Transfer 1. Scope of the Technology: All rights and interests, whether existing now or arising in the future, relating to the product, including but not limited to the product formula, manufacturing process, technical requirements and all technical materials relating to the product; all documents relating to the registration application; and all related rights and interests, including rights of use, ownership, transfer, production and sale. “Appendix 1: Complete List of Technical Materials to Be Delivered” and “Appendix 2: Acceptance Standards for Three Batches of Qualified Products” shall constitute integral parts of this Agreement. Page 1 Party B warrants that it independently and fully owns the product formula, process, registration materials and Health Food Registration Certificate, free and clear of co-ownership, mortgage, pledge, exclusive third-party license, intellectual property dispute or other defects in title. Any dispute over ownership shall constitute a material breach by Party B. 2. Technical Indicators and Parameters: As set forth in the technical materials to be delivered. 3. Level of Industrial Development of the technical know-how: Pilot-scale testing. Article 2. Rights and Obligations of Party A and Party B 1. Rights of Party A (1) To inquire of Party B at any time regarding the implementation progress of each stage of the product, any problems encountered and proposed solutions; (2) To consult Party B at any time regarding the technology relating to the product and applicable laws and regulations. 2. Obligations of Party A (1) To pay the relevant fees to Party B in accordance with the terms of this Agreement; (2) Party A shall hold, or shall provide, a Health Food SC Certificate or other relevant qualifications for the applicable dosage form for the factory engaged by Party A or its cooperating contract manufacturer; (3) To determine the name of the company that will be the transferee of the product within ten (10) working days before notarization of this Agreement; (3) To confirm the technical content of the product, including its formula, manufacturing process and technical requirements, at the times agreed in this Agreement; (4) To be responsible for handling matters in connection with the transfer of the product, including but not limited to notarization of this Agreement, sample trial production, sample testing, review, re-examination, hygienic testing, stability testing, tests of functional ingredients, samples for review meetings and dynamic on-site inspections, and to bear the related costs; (5) If Party A’s corporate information changes, including but not limited to its company name, legal representative or registered address, to notify Party B in writing within five (5) working days. Page 2 3. Obligations of Party B (1) To provide the complete set of registration application materials and supplemental materials for the product; (2) To review the hygienic, stability and functional-ingredient test reports and the full-item testing report for the product, and to standardize, compile and provide the complete set of technology transfer materials and supplemental materials; (3) To provide qualification documents required under the Administrative Measures for the Registration and Filing of Health Foods; (4) To be responsible for technical issues arising during the transfer of the product, and to promptly supplement materials and respond to review comments raised by review authorities at all levels and experts, until Party A obtains the Domestic Health Food Registration Certificate for the product; (5) To keep Party A informed of implementation progress at each stage of the product, any problems encountered and proposed solutions; (6) To provide Party A, free of charge and as needed, with consulting services concerning the technology relating to the product and applicable laws and regulations; (7) To assist with all transfer procedures relating to Party A’s obtaining the Domestic Health Food Registration Certificate for the product; (8) To arrange and assist testing institutions in completing any additional tests required by applicable regulations for the product (including, if applicable, safety toxicology testing and functional testing). Party B shall provide complete registration materials on time and cooperate with the transfer procedures. Article 3. Time, Place and Method for Party B’s Delivery of Technical Materials 1. Delivery Time: As specified in the relevant provisions concerning the payment method under this Agreement. 2. Delivery Place: Beijing (or by express courier to Party A’s mailing address set forth in this Agreement). If Party B delays delivery of the complete set of technical materials, Party A shall have the right to defer the corresponding installment payment, and such deferral shall not be deemed late payment by Party A or give rise to the liquidated damages under Paragraph 1 of Article 7. For delivery by mail, Party B shall bear the risk of loss, damage or omission of materials in transit and shall reorganize and resend the complete materials free of charge. 3. Delivery Method: The parties shall verify the materials and sign the relevant handover documents. Page 3 Article 4. Status of the Technology Before Effectiveness of this Agreement During the research and development of this project, Party B conducted technology research on a laboratory and pilot scale, and did not engage in actual commercial production of the product. Party B undertakes that it has not authorized, transferred or licensed the technology to any third party. If Party B conceals any history of commercialization or external authorization, such concealment shall constitute a material breach by Party B, and Party A may terminate this Agreement and require Party B to refund twice the amount already paid. Article 5. Technical Services and Guidance To ensure that Party A can effectively implement the technology, Party B shall provide the following technical services and guidance to Party A: 1. Content of Technical Services and Guidance: To guide Party A in producing three batches of qualified products and to provide consultation and guidance regarding the product. “Qualified products” means that Party A is able to complete pilot-scale production in accordance with the formula and process approved by the State, continuously produce three batches that meet the technical requirements, and pass accelerated stability testing. 2. Method of Technical Services and Guidance: By telephone or correspondence, and, where necessary, by dispatching technical personnel to provide on-site guidance. Party A shall bear the travel expenses of Party B’s technical personnel. Article 6. Technology Transfer Fee and Payment Method 1. The total technology (transfer) fee shall be RMB 1,550,000. 2. Party A shall pay the technology transfer fee to Party B in installments, as follows: (1) Within five (5) working days after this Agreement becomes effective, Party A shall pay Party B the first installment of RMB 465,000. Upon receipt of the payment, Party A and Party B shall notarize this Agreement and sign a commissioned processing and sales agreement; (2) Within five (5) working days after Party A has continuously produced three batches of qualified samples, Party A shall pay Party B the second installment of RMB 1,007,500. Within five (5) working days after receipt of such payment, Party B shall deliver to Party A the original Domestic Health Food Registration Certificate for the product; Page 4 (3) Within five (5) working days after Party A receives the Health Food Acceptance Notice for the product issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation, Party A shall pay Party B the third installment of RMB 77,500. If Party B fails to deliver the original registration certificate or the technical materials are incomplete, Party A shall have the right to suspend the corresponding installment payment, and such suspension shall not constitute late payment by Party A. (4) Party B’s bank name, address and account number are as follows: [Bank details redacted.] (5) Party B shall issue an ordinary value-added tax invoice to Party A. Article 7. Other Agreements Regarding Relevant Expenses 1. If Party A delays payment, it shall pay Party B liquidated damages at the rate of 0.03% of the amount then due and unpaid for each day of delay. If Party A remains unable to pay the contractual amount within thirty (30) working days after the payment deadline specified in this Agreement, Party A shall be deemed to have waived its right to acquire the subject matter of this Agreement, and Party B shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time. Fees already paid by Party A shall not be refunded. 2. If Party B delays delivery of materials or the registration certificate, or refuses to cooperate with the review process, Party B shall pay Party A liquidated damages for each day of delay at the rate of 0.03% of the corresponding installment amount. If Party B’s delay exceeds thirty (30) working days, Party A may unilaterally terminate this Agreement, and Party B shall refund all amounts paid and compensate Party A for its losses; 3. If additional testing is required during the transfer because the product’s dosage form shares test reports with other products, Party B shall arrange and pay for such testing; 4. If test reports that were not required under the regulations in effect at the time of Party B’s initial registration application must be supplemented during the transfer of the product, Party B shall arrange the testing and Party A shall bear the related costs; 5. If test reports need to be prepared again during the transfer of the product because the testing methods are adjusted in accordance with national policies or regulations, Party B shall arrange the testing and Party A shall bear the costs. Page 5 Article 8. Project Contacts During the term of this Agreement, both parties shall appoint contact persons. The project contacts shall be responsible for the following: 1. Inquiring about the performance of this Agreement; 2. Promptly completing coordination matters between the parties; 3. Handling other related matters as necessary. (1) If either party changes its project contact, contact information or mailing address, it shall notify the other party in writing within five (5) working days. If failure to give timely notice affects the performance of this Agreement or causes losses, the responsible party shall bear the corresponding liability; (2) If the corporate information of either Party A or Party B changes, including but not limited to its company name, legal representative or registered address, it shall notify Party B in writing within five (5) working days. If failure to give timely notice affects the performance of this Agreement or causes losses, the responsible party shall bear the corresponding liability. Article 9. Force Majeure and Material Changes in National Policies If a force majeure event or a material change in national policies renders performance of this Agreement unnecessary or impossible, neither party shall be liable for breach, and the parties shall consult with each other regarding termination of this Agreement. Any losses resulting therefrom shall be borne separately by each party. Amounts already paid shall not be refunded, and unpaid amounts shall no longer be payable. Article 10. Other Agreements 1. Party A shall complete the processing of qualified samples of the product within one hundred and twenty (120) working days from the date on which Party B has delivered the complete set of technical materials and the parties have signed the materials handover list. If, within the foregoing period, Party A raises written objections concerning product quality or technical parameters and, after Party B makes corrections, the product still fails to meet the qualification standards, the parties shall terminate this Agreement and Party B shall refund all transfer fees paid by Party A in full; Page 6 2. If, within one (1) year after execution of this Agreement, Party A has not obtained the Health Food Acceptance Notice issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation, Party A shall pay all remaining amounts due under this Agreement within five (5) working days; (1) If acceptance cannot be obtained due to reasons attributable to Party A, including Party A’s failure to provide its corporate qualifications on time, refusal to cooperate with sample trial production or lack of its own qualifications, Party A’s payment of the remaining balance shall be deferred; (2) If Party A is unable to obtain acceptance because Party B delays delivery of materials or the registration certificate, Paragraph 2 of Article 7 shall apply, and Party B shall also pay liquidated damages equal to twenty percent (20%) of the total contract amount. (3) If acceptance is delayed for reasons attributable to neither party, such as a backlog in national review or temporary policy adjustments, the parties shall consult to extend the acceptance period, and the deadline for Party A to pay the remaining balance shall be extended accordingly. 3. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the applicable measures, Party B undertakes that it has not previously manufactured or sold, and will not in the future manufacture or sell, the product. Party B has the exclusive right to transfer the technology for the product contemplated under this Agreement. Upon completion of the technology transfer under this Agreement, Party A shall own all rights and interests relating to the product, and Party B shall no longer have any rights in the subject matter of this Agreement; 4. During the performance of this Agreement, Party B shall not enter into an identical transfer of the subject matter of this Agreement with any third party. If Party B violates this provision, in addition to refunding the amounts already paid by Party A, Party B shall compensate Party A in an amount equal to twice the amounts paid; 5. If the transfer cannot be completed for reasons attributable to Party B, within one (1) week after the product is announced as not approved on the website of the Center for Food Evaluation of the State Administration for Market Regulation, Party A shall return all materials provided by Party B (including the original approval certificate) and undertake not to use the technology owned by Party B to manufacture or develop the same product. Party B shall refund all amounts received from Party A and bear all actual expenses incurred by Party A for notarization, samples, testing and review. Party B shall independently handle the issuance of red-letter invoices for any invoices already issued and shall bear all tax losses, which may not be deducted from the refund. 6. If the transfer cannot be completed for reasons attributable to Party A, Party A may, within ninety (90) working days, designate a third party as the transferee to succeed to Party A’s rights and obligations under this Agreement, and Party B shall continue to cooperate in handling the relevant transfer procedures. Otherwise, Party B shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, and amounts already paid by Party A shall not be refunded. Page 7 7. Both parties agree to keep confidential all matters under this Agreement and all confidential information involved herein, and neither party may disclose or make such information available to any third party without the consent of the rights holder. The confidentiality obligations shall survive termination of this Agreement and remain effective until all information required to be kept confidential lawfully enters the public domain. A party breaching this provision shall compensate the other party for the losses caused thereby; Article 11. Termination of the Agreement After the parties have performed the relevant provisions of this Agreement, this Agreement shall terminate once Party A has obtained the Domestic Health Food Registration Certificate and paid all amounts due under this Agreement to Party B. Party B shall not be responsible for any benefits or losses of Party A after Party A obtains the Domestic Health Food Registration Certificate. For supplements, amendments or other related matters arising from changes in national policies or changes by Party A to its requirements for the product, as well as any subsequent renewal of registration, Party A may separately engage Party B upon consultation. Article 12. Dispute Resolution Any dispute arising from the performance of this Agreement shall be resolved through consultation or mediation between the parties. If consultation or mediation fails, either party may bring a lawsuit before the people’s court at the location of the plaintiff in accordance with law. Article 13. Counterparts This Agreement is executed in six (6) originals, three (3) for Party A and three (3) for Party B, each of which shall have the same legal effect. Article 14. Effectiveness This Agreement shall become effective upon signature and affixation of seals by both parties. Party A: Hubei Taihe Biotechnology Co., Ltd. Legal Representative/Authorized Representative (Signature) Date: November 17, 2026 Party B: Harbin Aikesailun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. Legal Representative/Authorized Representative: (Signature) Date: November 17, 2026 Page 8

title: POWER SOLUTIONS INTERNATIONAL, INC.
text: EX-10.1 2 d163385dex101.htm EX-10.1 EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 ANCHOR RESOURCE MANAGEMENT Interim CFO Contractual Agreement Client: Power Solutions International Location: Itasca, IL Prepared by: Anchor Resource Management Project Lead: Robert Losier, Managing Partner – Financial Services Proposed Start Date: Monday, November 16, 2026 Overview Anchor Resource Management appreciates the opportunity to support Power Solutions International (PSI) in addressing the financial challenges at Power Solutions International in Itasca, Illinois. In follow up to our conversations for the requirement of an immediate interim CFO support PSI is considering, please find below the scope of work that was identified during our conversation and the terms and conditions of how the scope will be achieved. This effort will be done in a timely manner that will impact and align with shareholder expectations. We appreciate the opportunity to submit this contractual agreement to stabilize and enhance the company for the future. We are sending this contract to confirm our understanding of the support we will provide. Scope of Work Robert Losier, of Anchor, will report directly to the CEO, Richard Hu, and will perform the following activities: • Financial oversight : cash flow, liquidity, budgets, forecasts, financial reporting, and performance analysis. • Controls and compliance : accounting close, year-end close, internal controls, audit coordination, tax and regulatory deadlines, and risk escalation. • Leadership : managing finance staff and working with the CEO, board, lenders, auditors, and department heads. • Decision support : evaluating spending, pricing, hiring, investments, financing, and other major business choices. • Transition work : assessing the finance function, documenting key processes, identifying urgent issues, and supporting the permanent CFO’s onboarding. CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY | Anchor Resource Management – This contract and all accompanying materials contain confidential and proprietary information belonging to Anchor Resource Management. They are provided solely for the confidential evaluation of the proposed engagement by the intended recipient and may not be copied, disclosed, distributed, or used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of Anchor Resource Management. © 2026 Anchor Resource Management. All Rights Reserved. 1 ½ Page Project Timeline Anticipated Start Date: Monday, November 16, 2026 The engagement will continue on a weekly basis until concluded by mutual agreement between Anchor Resource Management and PSI. Priorities and duration will be evaluated as the engagement progresses. Anchor requires, in writing, a 30-day termination notice. Staffing and Professional Investment Anchor has identified Robert Losier as Interim CFO to lead the work listed in the scope above. Robert is a well-seasoned CFO, with public and private company experience across the automotive, industrial and financial sectors. For the first week following the start date, Robert will be assessing the situation with PSI and understanding the full capacity and responsibilities which he will be serving. For this reason, we propose a weekly rate of $40,000. A retainer of $80,000 is required to start the engagement. The retainer will be credited against professional fees and approved project-related expenses applied to the final invoices of the engagement. In addition to professional fees, reasonable project-related travel and living expenses will be reimbursable, including: • Commercial airfare • Hotel accommodations • Rental vehicles and ground transportation • Meals • Other reasonable project-related expenses Travel and other reimbursable expenses will be charged at actual cost. Any applicable expense approval requirements will be coordinated with PSI. Billing & Payment Terms Billing Frequency: Weekly, with invoices reflecting professional services performed and approved reimbursable expenses incurred. Payment Terms: Net 15 days from the invoice date. CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY | Anchor Resource Management – This contract and all accompanying materials contain confidential and proprietary information belonging to Anchor Resource Management. They are provided solely for the confidential evaluation of the proposed engagement by the intended recipient and may not be copied, disclosed, distributed, or used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of Anchor Resource Management. © 2026 Anchor Resource Management. All Rights Reserved. 2 ½ Page Authorization to Proceed Anchor Resource Management appreciates the opportunity to support PSI during this period. We look forward to working collaboratively with your team to strengthen execution, improve performance, and establish sustainable operating practices. If the terms and conditions of this contract, including General Terms and Conditions, are acceptable to you, kindly indicate your acceptance by signing below and return it to my attention via email. We appreciate the opportunity to submit this contract to work alongside you and your team. Accepted By: Power Solutions International Anchor Resource Management Name: Nan (Richard) Hu Name: Robert Losier Title: Chief Executive Officer Title: Managing Partner – Financial Services Signature: /s/ Nan (Richard) Hu Signature: /s/ Robert Losier Date: 11/15/2026 Date: 11/14/2026 CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY | Anchor Resource Management – This contract and all accompanying materials contain confidential and proprietary information belonging to Anchor Resource Management. They are provided solely for the confidential evaluation of the proposed engagement by the intended recipient and may not be copied, disclosed, distributed, or used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of Anchor Resource Management. © 2026 Anchor Resource Management. All Rights Reserved. 3 ½ Page GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS These General Terms and Conditions (“Terms”) are incorporated into this Agreement to which these Terms of such services shall be as set forth herein. 1. All representatives of ANCHOR supplied by it to perform its consulting services hereunder shall be employees of ANCHOR. The parties intend that an independent contractor relationship will be created by this agreement. Neither ANCHOR nor any of its representatives will be considered an employee or agent of Client. Therefore, all payroll taxes and employee benefits with respect to representatives of ANCHOR are the responsibility of ANCHOR. ANCHOR is a Tennessee corporation and as such abides by employment laws applicable to Tennessee corporations. 2. Client agrees not to make an offer of employment to, or hire as an independent contractor, any ANCHOR personnel for a period of 365 days after completion of the assignment. In the event Client desires to extend an offer of employment to or hire as an independent contractor, an ANCHOR employee, either while on assignment to the Client or before expiration of the 365 days, the Client shall contact ANCHOR and make such a request. If the Client and the ANCHOR representative reach any such agreement, the Client shall pay to ANCHOR a one-time fee equal to 50% of the agreed upon first year’s salary or contract unless ANCHOR otherwise agrees to reduce or waive such fee. 3. All amounts invoiced is not contingent upon the outcome of any work performed or analytical conclusions set forth in any work products or the results achieved. If any fees and/or expenses are not paid by the Company by the relevant due date, ANCHOR may reserve the right to charge interest on the unpaid amount until payment is made in full. Calculation of interest may be one percent (1%) of fees and/or expense amount due per month until the balance is resolved. 4. ANCHOR has previously executed a confidentiality agreement with respect to its work with Client and its affiliates and such agreement shall remain in full force and effect following the execution and delivery of this agreement. This agreement, together with the confidentiality agreement, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. All notices required or permitted to be delivered under this agreement shall be addressed to ANCHOR at 127 S. Water Ave. Gallatin, TN 37066. 5. This Agreement may be terminated at any time by written notice by one party to the other; however, notwithstanding such termination, ANCHOR is entitled to all fees and expenses due under the provisions of this Agreement. Payment shall be remitted promptly, as reasonably practicable (and in any event, within thirty (30) days following such termination). They are provided solely for the confidential evaluation of the proposed engagement by the intended recipient and may not be copied, disclosed, distributed, or used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of Anchor Resource Management. © 2026 Anchor Resource Management. All Rights Reserved. 4 ½ Page 6. The indemnified ANCHOR parties shall not be liable to the Client, Company, or any party asserting claims on behalf of the Company except for direct damages found in a final determination to be the direct result of the gross negligence or intentional misconduct of ANCHOR or its personnel. The indemnified ANCHOR parties shall not be liable for incidental, indirect, special or consequential damages (i.e. lost profits) arising out of, or in connection with this Agreement, under any circumstances, even if the indemnified ANCHOR parties have been advised of the possibility of such damages. The Indemnified ANCHOR parties aggregate liability, contract, or otherwise, is limited to the amount of fees paid to ANCHOR for services on this engagement (the” Liability Cap”). The Liability Cap is the total limit of the Indemnified ANCHOR parties’ aggregate liability for any and all claims or demands by anyone pursuant to this Agreement, including liability to the Company, to any other parties hereto, and to any others making claims relating to the work performed by ANCHOR pursuant to this Agreement. Any such claimants shall allocate any amounts payable by the Indemnified ANCHOR parties among themselves as appropriate, but if they cannot agree on the allocation it will not affect the enforceability of the Liability Cap. Under no circumstances shall the aggregate of all such allocations or other claims against the indemnified ANCHOR parties pursuant to this Agreement exceed the Liability Cap. The Company accepts and acknowledges that any legal proceedings arising from or in connection with this Agreement (or any variation or addition thereto) must be commenced within one (1) year from the date when the Company becomes aware of or ought reasonably to have become aware of the facts, which give rise to ANCHOR’s alleged liability. The Company also agrees that no action or claims will be brought against any ANCHOR employees personally in connection with such employees providing services pursuant to this Agreement. 7. Any dispute, claim or controversy arising out of relating to this Agreement or the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation or validity thereof that is not settled to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties within the applicable notice including the determination of the scope or applicability of this Agreement to arbitrate, shall be resolved by arbitration between the Parties. No form of discovery, including but not limited to interrogatories, requests for admissions, or depositions, shall be permitted. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding upon the Parties and shall be set forth in a written reasoned opinion, and any award may be enforced by either Party in a court of competent jurisdiction. The arbitrators may award costs and attorneys’ fees to the prevailing party. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction. In any court proceeding arising out of this Agreement, the parties hereby waive any right to trial by jury. 8. The Company agrees that, when the engagement is completed, ANCHOR may, at its option and expense, place announcements and advertisements or otherwise publicize the engagement and ANCHOR’s role and involvement (which may include the reproduction of the Company’s logo and a hyperlink to the Company’s website) on ANCHOR’s website and any ANCHOR related material. They are provided solely for the confidential evaluation of the proposed engagement by the intended recipient and may not be copied, disclosed, distributed, or used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of Anchor Resource Management. © 2026 Anchor Resource Management. All Rights Reserved. 5 ½ Page RIDER TO INTERIM CFO CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENT This Rider is entered into as of November 14th, 2026, between Power Solutions International, Inc. , a Delaware corporation (“ PSI ”), and Anchor Resource Management , a Tennessee corporation (“ Anchor ”). It amends the Interim CFO Contractual Agreement accepted by Anchor on November 14, 2026, including its General Terms and Conditions (the “ Agreement ”). This Rider controls over any conflicting term. “Client” and “Company” mean PSI. “Paragraph” means a numbered paragraph of the General Terms and Conditions. 1. Officer Role. Robert Losier (the “ Interim CFO ”) will begin services once PSI’s Board appoints him Interim Chief Financial Officer. Despite Paragraph 1, while appointed he is an officer and agent of PSI and owes PSI the duties of an officer. He remains Anchor’s employee for payroll, tax, and benefits purposes. He will work full-time and mainly on-site in Itasca, Illinois. Anchor may not replace him without PSI’s written consent. 2. Fees and Payment. (a) The fee is a fixed $40,000 per week for the entire engagement. Partial weeks are prorated at $8,000 per business day. (b) Expenses must follow PSI’s travel policy. Any expense over $2,500 needs PSI’s prior written approval. (c) PSI will pay undisputed amounts within 30 days after it receives an invoice. Interest under Paragraph 3 does not apply to amounts PSI disputes in good faith. (d) Anchor will refund any unapplied part of the $80,000 retainer within 30 days after the engagement ends. 3. Termination. This Section 3 replaces the “Project Timeline” termination sentence and Paragraph 5. (a) PSI may terminate on seven days’ written notice. (b) PSI may terminate immediately for material breach, misconduct, or violation of law or PSI policy. (c) Anchor may terminate on 30 days’ written notice. (d) After termination, PSI owes only fees through the termination date and approved expenses. (e) On termination, the Interim CFO will resign all PSI offices and return PSI records. 4. Compliance and Disclosure. (a) The Interim CFO will comply with PSI’s Code of Conduct, Insider Trading Policy, and other policies that apply to executive officers. (b) He will sign the certifications PSI requires of its principal financial officer, including those under Sections 302 and 906 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. (c) The confidentiality agreement in Paragraph 4 binds the Interim CFO personally and covers material nonpublic information. (d) Despite the “Confidential & Proprietary” legend, PSI may disclose and publicly file the Agreement as required by law, SEC rules, or Nasdaq rules. Anchor will provide the information PSI needs for those filings. 5. Liability. This Section 5 replaces Paragraph 6. (a) Neither party is liable for consequential damages. (b) Each party’s total liability is capped at the greater of fees paid and payable or $2,000,000. (c) The exclusion and cap do not apply to: (i) breach of confidentiality; (ii) fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct; or (iii) Anchor’s indemnity in Section 6. (d) Nothing in the Agreement limits PSI’s claims against the Interim CFO as an officer, or shortens any statute of limitations. (e) PSI does not indemnify Anchor. 6. Indemnity and Insurance. (a) Anchor will indemnify PSI against third-party claims arising from: (i) employment, tax, or benefits matters concerning Anchor personnel; or (ii) Anchor’s breach of confidentiality, gross negligence, or willful misconduct. (b) PSI will cover the Interim CFO under its officer indemnification and D&O insurance on the same terms as its other executive officers. (c) Anchor will carry professional liability insurance of at least $2,000,000. 7. Hiring Fee. This Section 7 replaces Paragraph 2. PSI may hire the Interim CFO at any time. If it does so during the engagement or within 12 months after it ends, PSI will pay Anchor a fee based on his first-year base pay: (a) 20% if the hire occurs before week 26 of the engagement; (b) 10% if it occurs in weeks 26 through 52; and (c) nothing after week 52. 8. Publicity. This Section 8 replaces Paragraph 8. Anchor may not use PSI’s name or logo, or publicize the engagement, without PSI’s prior written consent. 9. Governing Law and Disputes. Illinois law governs the Agreement. Arbitration under Paragraph 7 will be administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Rules, before one arbitrator, in Chicago. The no-discovery sentence is deleted, and the arbitrator may allow reasonable discovery. 10. General. (a) PSI owns all work product created for PSI. (b) For two years after the engagement ends, Anchor will reasonably cooperate with audits, regulatory inquiries, and litigation, at a reasonable hourly rate. (c) Notices to PSI go to 1465 Hamilton Parkway, Itasca, IL 60143IL, Attention: General Counsel. (d) Except as amended by this Rider, the Agreement remains in effect. [Signature page follows] POWER SOLUTIONS INTERNATIONAL, INC. title: PharmaCyte Biotech, Inc.
text: EX-10.1 2 pharmacyte_ex1001.htm CONSENT AND WARRANT EXCHANGE AGREEMENT Exhibit 10.1 CONSENT AND WARRANT EXCHANGE AGREEMENT This CONSENT AND WARRANT EXCHANGE AGREEMENT (this “ Agreement ”) is made effective as of November 15, 2026, by and between Q/C Technologies, Inc. (the “ Company ”) and PharmaCyte Biotech, Inc. (the “ Holder ”), in its capacity as the holder of the Warrants (as defined below) and of the Holder Series H Shares (as defined below). RECITALS WHEREAS , on May 20, 2024, the Company entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement (the “ Series G Purchase Agreement ”), pursuant to which the Company sold long-term warrants (the “ Series G Long-Term Warrants ”) to acquire up to 3,854,626 shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the “ Common Stock ”); WHEREAS , the Holder acquired and is the record and beneficial owner of 2,076,351 Series G Long-Term Warrants (the “ Warrants ”); WHEREAS , the Company has outstanding shares of its Series H Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.001 per share (the “ Series H Preferred Stock ”), issued pursuant to the Certificate of Designations of Series H Convertible Preferred Stock filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated September 1, 2025, as amended by the Certificate of Amendment thereto dated October 3, 2025 (as amended, the “ Series H Certificate of Designations ”), which provides for a “Maturity Date” (as defined therein) of March 2, 2027, and which may be amended with the vote or written consent of the Required Holders (as defined in the Series H Certificate of Designations), voting separately as a single class; WHEREAS , the Holder is the record and beneficial owner of 3,000,000 shares of Series H Preferred Stock (the “ Holder Series H Shares ”), which constitute more than a majority of the outstanding shares of Series H Preferred Stock and, accordingly, the Required Holders; and WHEREAS , the Company and the Holder have agreed to enter into this Agreement pursuant to which, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing (as defined below) and the other terms of this Agreement, (i) 851,304 Series G Long-Term Warrants (collectively, the “ Exchange Warrants ”) and the rights and obligations of the Holder thereunder will be exchanged for 4,982,272 shares of Common Stock (the “ Shares ”), with all Warrants other than the Exchange Warrants remaining outstanding in accordance with their terms, and (ii) the Holder, as a holder of Series H Preferred Stock, will consent to the extension of the Maturity Date of the Series H Preferred Stock by six (6) months, as set forth in Section 1.03 . NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the foregoing premises and the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which are hereby acknowledged, intending to be legally bound, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1 AGREEMENT ARTICLE I. EXCHANGE 1.01 The Exchange . At the Closing (as defined below), the Company and the Holder shall, pursuant to Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “ Securities Act ”), exchange the Exchange Warrants for the Shares (the “ Exchange ”), as described herein. (a) Closing . Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by the Holder in its sole discretion) of the conditions set forth in Section 1.02 and the other terms of this Agreement, the closing of the Exchange (the “ Closing ”) shall occur remotely upon, and shall be deemed to occur simultaneously with, the actual delivery of all of the Shares to the Holder or its designee in accordance with Section 1.01(c) (the date of such delivery, the “ Closing Date ”). The Holder shall not be required to surrender or deliver the Exchange Warrants before the Shares have been actually delivered to the Holder or its designee as provided herein. The Company’s delivery of the Shares and the Holder’s surrender or deemed surrender of the Exchange Warrants are concurrent conditions to the effectiveness of the Exchange and cancellation of the Exchange Warrants, and no Exchange Warrant shall be deemed surrendered, cancelled or extinguished before such actual delivery. The Holder acknowledges that immediately following the Exchange, the Holder is deemed an “affiliate” of the Company, as such term is defined in Rule 144(a)(1) promulgated under the Securities Act. (b) Consideration . At the Closing, the Shares shall be issued to Holder solely in exchange for the Exchange Warrants, without payment of any additional consideration by such Holder that would not be consistent with the application of Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Company’s obligations under the Exchange Warrants shall not be terminated, cancelled or waived, and no Exchange Warrant shall be deemed surrendered or extinguished, until Holder has actually received all Shares required under this Agreement. Upon such actual receipt, the Exchange Warrants shall be deemed surrendered and cancelled, and Holder shall deliver or cause to be delivered the original Exchange Warrants in accordance with Section 1.01(c); this Section 1.01(b) shall constitute an instrument of termination and cancellation effective upon such actual receipt, without affecting any claim or remedy arising before or from the Company’s failure to perform this Agreement. (c) Delivery . The Company shall deliver or cause its transfer agent (the “ Transfer Agent ”) to deliver the Shares to Holder or its designee in certificated or other book-entry form no later than two (2) business days after the date on which the conditions set forth in Section 1.02 have been satisfied (or waived by the Holder), and such delivery shall constitute the Closing. Prior to such delivery, the Company shall deliver an irrevocable instruction letter to the Transfer Agent, acknowledged by the Transfer Agent, directing the issuance, delivery, and holding-period tacking contemplated by this Agreement, and the Company shall bear all reasonable transfer-agent, legal-opinion, and other costs of issuance and delivery. The Holder shall deliver or cause to be delivered to the Company (or its designee), within five (5) trading days after Holder’s actual receipt of all Shares, the original Exchange Warrants. (d) Tacking . The holding period of the Shares for purposes of Rule 144 and Section 4(a)(1) of the Securities Act tacks on to the holding period of the Exchange Warrants. (e) Other Documents . The Company and the Holder shall execute and/or deliver such other documents and agreements as are reasonably necessary to effectuate the Exchange pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. 2 1.02 Conditions to Holder’s Closing Obligation . The Holder’s obligation to consummate the Exchange, including its obligation to surrender the Exchange Warrants, is subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by the Holder in its sole discretion) on or before the Closing of each of the following conditions: (a) The Company shall have executed and delivered this Agreement and all other documents required hereunder, including the irrevocable instruction letter to the Transfer Agent specified in Section 1.01(c). (b) The representations and warranties of the Company shall be true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing, and the Company shall have performed in all material respects all covenants and obligations required to be performed at or before the Closing. (c) The Shares shall have been approved for listing on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“ Nasdaq ”) (or the principal Nasdaq market on which the Common Stock is then listed), subject only to official notice of issuance, and trading of the Common Stock shall not have been suspended or threatened in writing with suspension by Nasdaq or the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”). (d) No law, order or injunction shall prohibit the Exchange, and no event shall have occurred since the date hereof that has materially impaired, or would reasonably be expected to materially impair, the Company’s ability to issue, deliver, list or permit the transfer of the Shares or perform its obligations under this Agreement. 1.03 Maturity Date Extension . The Holder, in its capacity as the holder of the Holder Series H Shares and for purposes of Section 32(b) of the Series H Certificate of Designations and Section 228 of the Delaware General Corporation Law (the “ DGCL ”), hereby irrevocably consents to, approves and adopts amending and restating Section 33(jj) of the Series H Certificate of Designations to read: “Maturity Date” shall mean September 2, 2027; provided, however, the Maturity Date may be extended upon the mutual consent of a Holder and the Company with respect to such Holder; and provided further, however, the Maturity Date may be extended at the option of a Holder with respect to such Holder (i) in the event that, and for so long as, a Triggering Event shall have occurred and be continuing or any event shall have occurred and be continuing that with the passage of time and the failure to cure would result in a Triggering Event or (ii) through the date that is twenty (20) Business Days after the consummation of a Fundamental Transaction in the event that a Fundamental Transaction is publicly announced or a Change of Control Notice is delivered prior to the Maturity Date, provided further that if a Holder elects to convert some or all of its Preferred Shares pursuant to Section 4 hereof, and the Conversion Amount would be limited pursuant to Section 4(d) hereunder, the Maturity Date shall automatically be extended until such time as such provision shall not limit the conversion of such Preferred Shares. Such consent shall constitute the written consent without a meeting of the Required Holders, voting separately as a single class (the “ Required Holder Consent ”). 3 1.04 Demand Registration Rights . The Company shall, upon Holder’s written demand made at any time after ninety (90) days following the Closing (the “ Demand ”), promptly, and in any event within thirty (30) days after receipt of the Demand, file with the SEC a registration statement covering the resale by Holder of all Shares then held by Holder (the “ Registration Statement ”), and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause the Registration Statement to become effective as soon as practicable after such filing and to remain effective and available for use continuously until the earlier of (A) the date on which all Shares covered by the Registration Statement have been sold or (B) the date on which all such Shares may be sold by Holder pursuant to Rule 144 under the Securities Act (or any successor rule thereto), without any requirement that the Company comply with Rule 144(c) (or any successor provision) and without any volume, manner-of-sale, or current public information limitations; provided that the Company shall promptly prepare and file with the SEC such amendments and supplements to the Registration Statement and the related prospectus as may be necessary to keep the Registration Statement effective and available for use throughout and to comply with applicable securities laws. The Company shall promptly notify Holder in writing (i) when the Registration Statement is filed and when it is declared effective, (ii) of any request by the SEC for an amendment or supplement to the Registration Statement or related prospectus or for additional information, (iii) of the issuance by the SEC of any stop order or the initiation of any proceeding for that purpose, (iv) of any event that causes the Registration Statement or related prospectus to contain an untrue statement of a material fact or omit a material fact necessary to make the statements therein not misleading, and (v) of any suspension of the use of the Registration Statement permitted below and the date on which such suspension ends, and shall promptly furnish Holder with copies of all such amendments, supplements, and notices. The Company may suspend the use of the Registration Statement only (A) if the Company’s board of directors determines in good faith that continued use would require disclosure of material non-public information that would be materially prejudicial to the Company or its stockholders or would materially interfere with a bona fide material financing, acquisition, or similar corporate transaction, or (B) to the extent required by applicable securities laws or an SEC stop order; provided that any suspension under clause (A) shall be for the shortest period reasonably necessary and shall not exceed thirty (30) consecutive days or, in the aggregate, sixty (60) days in any twelve-month period, and no more than two (2) suspensions under clause (A) may occur in any twelve-month period. During any permitted suspension, the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to terminate the suspension as soon as practicable, and Holder may continue to sell Shares pursuant to Rule 144 or another available exemption. Upon receipt of a notice of a permitted suspension, Holder shall discontinue use of the Registration Statement until receipt of written notice from the Company that use may resume, and the Company shall promptly notify Holder when the Registration Statement is again available for use. The Company shall bear all reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incident to the registration contemplated hereby, including SEC and FINRA filing fees, Nasdaq listing fees, printing and distribution expenses, fees and disbursements of the Company’s counsel and independent public accountants, and the reasonable fees and disbursements of one counsel selected by Holder. The Company shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Holder, its directors, officers, partners, members, employees, agents, and representatives, and each person, if any, who controls Holder within the meaning of the Securities Act, from and against any loss, claim, damage, liability, cost, or expense (including reasonable attorneys’ fees and disbursements) arising out of or based upon (A) any untrue statement or alleged untrue statement of a material fact contained in the Registration Statement, any related prospectus, or any amendment or supplement thereto, or (B) any omission or alleged omission to state therein a material fact required to be stated or necessary to make the statements therein not misleading, except, in each case, to the extent that such loss, claim, damage, liability, cost, or expense results from information furnished in writing by Holder expressly for use therein; provided that the Company shall not be liable to the extent that any such loss, claim, damage, liability, cost, or expense results from Holder’s failure to deliver a current prospectus after the Company has furnished Holder with a corrected or supplemented prospectus. Holder shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Company, its directors, officers, agents, and representatives, and each person, if any, who controls the Company within the meaning of the Securities Act, from and against any loss, claim, damage, liability, cost, or expense arising out of or based upon any untrue statement or omission in the Registration Statement or related prospectus to the extent, but only to the extent, that such statement or omission was made in reliance upon and in conformity with information furnished in writing by Holder expressly for use therein; provided that Holder’s liability under this sentence shall not exceed the net proceeds received by Holder from sales pursuant to the Registration Statement. The rights and obligations set forth in this subsection shall survive the Closing and the surrender or cancellation of the Exchange Warrants. 4 ARTICLE II. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE COMPANY The Company represents and warrants to Holder as of the date hereof as follows: 2.01 Organization, Good Standing and Power . The Company is a corporation duly incorporated, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware and has the requisite corporate power to own, lease and operate its properties and assets and to conduct its business as it is now being conducted. 2.02 Authorization; Enforcement . The Company has the requisite corporate power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and to issue the Shares in accordance with the terms hereof. The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by the Company and the consummation by it of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary corporate action of the Company, and no further consent or authorization of the Company or its board of directors or stockholders is required, other than, with respect to the Series H Amendment, the Series H Resolutions and the Required Holder Consent described in Section 1.03 and Section 2.06. When executed and delivered by the Company, this Agreement shall constitute a valid and binding obligation of the Company, enforceable against the Company in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, reorganization, moratorium, liquidation, conservatorship, receivership or similar laws relating to, or affecting generally the enforcement of, creditor’s rights and remedies or by other equitable principles of general application. 2.03 Issuance of Shares . When the Shares are issued and delivered in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, the Shares shall be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable, free and clear of all liens, claims, security interests and other encumbrances, and free of any pre-emptive, participation, rights of first refusal or similar rights. The Company shall have reserved sufficient authorized and unissued Common Stock for the issuance and delivery of the Shares. 2.04 No Conflicts . The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by the Company and the consummation by the Company of the transactions contemplated hereby do not and will not: (i) conflict with or violate any provision of the Company’s certificate or articles of incorporation, bylaws or other organizational or charter documents; or (ii) conflict with, or constitute a default (or an event that with notice or lapse of time or both would become a default) under, result in the creation of any liens, claims, security interests, other encumbrances or defects upon any of the properties or assets of the Company in connection with, or give to others any rights of termination, amendment, acceleration or cancellation (with or without notice, lapse of time or both) of, any material agreement, credit facility, debt or other material instrument (evidencing Company debt or otherwise) or other material understanding to which such Company is a party or by which any property or asset of the Company is bound or affected; or (iii) conflict with or result in a violation of any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, injunction, decree or other restriction of any court or governmental authority to which the Company is subject (including federal and state securities laws and regulations), or by which any property or asset of the Company is bound or affected, except, in the case of each of clauses (ii) and (iii), such as could not have or reasonably be expected to result in a material adverse effect upon the business, prospects, properties, operations, condition (financial or otherwise) or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole, or in its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement. 2.05 Nasdaq Listing . The Company represents, warrants and covenants that it has taken, and will continue to take, all actions and make all filings necessary to cause the Shares to be approved for listing on Nasdaq, subject to official notice of issuance, to remain listed following the Closing. The Company shall promptly notify Holder of any notice of suspension, delisting or threatened suspension or delisting of the Common Stock or any refusal by Nasdaq to approve listing of the Shares. 5 2.06 Series H Amendment . The special committee of the Company’s board of directors, composed solely of directors who are disinterested with respect to the transactions contemplated hereby (the “ Special Committee ”), has duly adopted resolutions (the “ Series H Resolutions ”) approving and declaring advisable a certificate of amendment to the Series H Certificate of Designations amending and restating Section 33(jj) thereof as set forth in Section 1.03 (the “ Series H Amendment ”), and such resolutions are in full force and effect and have not been rescinded or modified. Upon the Required Holder Consent, the Series H Amendment has been duly approved in accordance with Section 242 of the DGCL, the Company’s certificate of incorporation and Section 32(b) of the Series H Certificate of Designations, and no other vote or consent of the holders of any class or series of the Company’s capital stock is required. The Company will file the Series H Amendment with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware within four (4) business days after the date hereof and will provide prompt notice of such action to the holders of Series H Preferred Stock that did not consent in writing as required by Section 228(e) of the DGCL. Upon such filing, the Series H Amendment will be effective, and the Maturity Date of the Series H Preferred Stock will be September 2, 2027. The Closing and the Exchange are not conditioned on the Series H Amendment, and no additional consideration shall be paid by the Holder in respect of the Series H Amendment. ARTICLE III. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE HOLDER The Holder represents and warrants to the Company as of the date hereof as follows: 3.01 Organization and Standing of the Holder . Holder is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its organization. 3.02 Authorization and Power . Holder has the requisite power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement. The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Holder and the consummation by it of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action, and no further consent or authorization of Holder or its board of directors or stockholders is required. When executed and delivered by Holder, this Agreement shall constitute the valid and binding obligations of Holder enforceable against Holder in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, liquidation, conservatorship, receivership or similar laws relating to, or affecting generally the enforcement of, creditor’s rights and remedies or by other equitable principles of general application. 3.03 Ownership of Holder Series H Shares . Holder is the record and beneficial owner of the Holder Series H Shares, which constitute a majority of the outstanding shares of Series H Preferred Stock, free and clear of any voting agreement, proxy or other restriction that would prevent Holder from delivering the consent set forth in Section 1.03. ARTICLE IV. MISCELLANEOUS 4.01 Amendment . No provision of this Agreement may be waived or amended except in a written instrument signed by the Company and Holder. 6 4.02 Notices . Any notice, demand, request, waiver or other communication required or permitted to be given hereunder shall be in writing and shall be effective (a) upon hand delivery by telecopy or facsimile at the address or number designated below (if delivered on a business day during normal business hours where such notice is to be received), or the first business day following such delivery (if delivered other than on a business day during normal business hours where such notice is to be received) or (b) on the second business day following the date of mailing by express courier service, fully prepaid, addressed to such address, or upon actual receipt of such mailing, whichever shall first occur or (c) upon delivery by e-mail (if delivered on a business day during normal business hours where such notice is to be received) upon recipient’s actual receipt and acknowledgement of such e-mail. The addresses for such communications shall be: If to the Company: Q/C Technologies, Inc. 333 Bush Street, Suite 1400 San Francisco, CA 94104 Attn: Joshua Silverman Title: Chief Executive Officer If to the Holder: PharmaCyte Biotech, Inc. 3960 Howard Hughes Parkway, Suite 500 Las Vegas, NV, 89169 Attn: Carlos Trujillo Title: Chief Financial Officer Any party hereto may from time to time change its address for notices by giving written notice of such changed address to the other party hereto. 4.03 Waivers . No waiver by either party of any default with respect to any provision, condition or requirement of this Agreement shall be deemed to be a continuing waiver in the future or a waiver of any other provision, condition or requirement hereof, nor shall any delay or omission of any party to exercise any right hereunder in any manner impair the exercise of any such right accruing to it thereafter. 4.04 Survival . All representations, warranties, covenants and agreements of the Company under this Agreement shall survive the Closing and the surrender or cancellation of the Exchange Warrants and remain in effect until fully performed or satisfied. 4.05 Headings . The article, section and subsection headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not constitute a part of this Agreement for any other purpose and shall not be deemed to limit or affect any of the provisions hereof. 4.06 Governing Law . This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to any of the conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the substantive law of another jurisdiction. 4.07 Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same instrument and shall become effective when counterparts have been signed by each party and delivered to the other parties hereto, it being understood that all parties need not sign the same counterpart. Signature pages to this Agreement may be delivered by facsimile or other means of electronic transmission. text: EX-10.2 3 ef20085888_ex10-2.htm EXHIBIT 10.2 Exhibit 10.2 TREELINE BIOSCIENCES, INC. POST-CLOSING EMPLOYEE STOCK PURCHASE PLAN 1. PURPOSE. The purpose of this Plan is to provide eligible employees of Standard BioTools Inc. (the “ Company ”) and the Participating Corporations with a means of acquiring an equity interest in the Company, to enhance such employees’ sense of participation in the affairs of the Company. Capitalized terms not defined elsewhere in the text are defined in Section 28 of this Plan. 2. ESTABLISHMENT OF PLAN. The Company proposes to grant rights to purchase shares of Common Stock to eligible employees of the Company and its Participating Corporations pursuant to this Plan. The Company intends this Plan to qualify as an “employee stock purchase plan” under Section 423 of the Code (including any amendments to or replacements of such Section), and this Plan shall be so construed, although the Company makes no undertaking or representation to maintain such qualification. Any term not expressly defined in this Plan but defined for purposes of Section 423 of the Code shall have the same definition herein. In addition, this Plan authorizes the grant of options under a Non-Section 423 Component that is not intended to meet Section 423 requirements, provided, to the extent necessary under Section 423 of the Code, the other terms and conditions of this Plan are met. Subject to Section 14 of this Plan, a total of 26,865,998 shares of Common Stock are reserved for issuance under this Plan. In addition, the number of shares of Common Stock available for grant and issuance under this Plan will be increased on January 1 st of each of the first ten (10) calendar years during the term of this Plan by the lesser of (i) one percent (1%) of the sum of (a) the total number of shares of all classes of the Company’s Common Stock; (b) the total number of shares of the Company’s Common Stock subject to Pre-Funded Warrants (if any); and (c) the number of shares of the Company’s Common Stock issuable upon conversion of any preferred stock (if any), in each case, issued and outstanding on each December 31 st immediately prior to the date of increase, rounded down to the next whole share, or (ii) such number of shares of Common Stock as may be determined by the Board or the Compensation Committee of the Board. Subject to Section 14 of this Plan, no more than 270,000,000 shares of Common Stock may be issued over the term of this Plan. For the avoidance of any uncertainty, shares of Common Stock withheld to satisfy tax withholding obligations shall not reduce the number of shares of Common Stock available for grant pursuant to this Plan and shall again be made available for grant pursuant to this Plan. The number of shares initially reserved for issuance under this Plan and the maximum number of shares that may be issued under this Plan shall be subject to adjustments effected in accordance with Section 14 of this Plan. Any or all such shares may be granted under the Section 423 Component. 3. ADMINISTRATION. This Plan will be administered by the Committee. The Committee may delegate administrative tasks under this Plan to a subcommittee or to one or more officers to assist with the administration of this Plan pursuant to specific delegation as permitted by applicable law. Subject to the provisions of this Plan and the limitations of Section 423 of the Code or any successor provision in the Code, all questions of interpretation or application of this Plan shall be determined by the Committee and its decisions shall be final and binding upon all eligible employees and Participants. The Committee will have full and exclusive discretionary authority to construe, interpret and apply the terms of this Plan, to determine eligibility (including that the Committee may determine that an employee of a third party agency who is providing services to a Participating Corporation at the direction of the Participating Corporation is eligible to participate in an Offering Period under the Non-Section 423 Component of this Plan), to designate the Participating Corporations, to determine whether Participating Corporations shall participate in the Section 423 Component or Non-Section 423 Component and to decide upon any and all claims filed under this Plan. Every finding, decision and determination made by the Committee will, to the full extent permitted by law, be final and binding upon all parties. Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in this Plan, the Committee may adopt rules, sub-plans, and/or procedures relating to the operation and administration of this Plan designed to facilitate compliance with local laws, regulations or customs or to achieve tax, securities law or other objectives for eligible employees outside of the United States. Further, the Committee is specifically authorized to adopt rules and procedures regarding the application of the definition of Compensation (as defined below) to Participants on payrolls outside of the United States, handling of Contributions, taking / making of other Contributions to this Plan, establishment of bank or trust accounts to hold Contributions, payment of interest, establishment of the exchange rate applicable to Contributions made in a currency other than U.S. dollars, obligations to pay payroll tax, determination of beneficiary designation requirements, tax withholding procedures, and handling of stock certificates that vary with applicable local requirements. The Committee will have the authority to determine the Fair Market Value of the Common Stock (which determination shall be final, binding and conclusive for all purposes) in accordance with Section 8 and Section 28(k) of this Plan and to interpret Section 8 and Section 28(k) of this Plan in connection with circumstances that impact the Fair Market Value. Members of the Committee shall receive no compensation for their services in connection with the administration of this Plan, other than standard fees as established from time to time by the Board for services rendered by Board members serving on Board committees. All expenses incurred in connection with the administration of this Plan shall be paid by the Company. For purposes of this Plan, the Committee may designate separate offerings under this Plan (the terms of which need not be identical) in which eligible employees of one or more Participating Corporations will participate, and the provisions of this Plan will separately apply to each such separate offering even if the dates of the applicable Offering Periods of each such offering are identical. To the extent permitted by Section 423 of the Code, the terms of each separate offering under this Plan need not be identical, provided that the rights and privileges established with respect to a particular offering are applied in an identical manner to all employees of every Participating Corporation whose employees are granted options under that particular offering. The Committee may establish rules to govern the terms of this Plan and the offering that will apply to Participants who transfer employment between the Company and Participating Corporations or between Participating Corporations, in accordance with requirements under Section 423 of the Code to the extent applicable. 4. ELIGIBILITY. (a) Any employee of the Company or the Participating Corporations is eligible to participate in an Offering Period under this Plan, except that one or more of the following categories of employees may be excluded from coverage under this Plan if determined by the Committee (other than where such exclusion is prohibited by applicable law): (i) employees who do not meet eligibility requirements that the Committee may choose to impose (within the limits permitted by the Code); (ii) employees who are not employed by the Company or a Participating Corporation prior to the beginning of such Offering Period or prior to such other time period as specified by the Committee; (iii) employees who have been employed less than two (2) years; (iv) employees who are customarily employed for twenty (20) or less hours per week; (v) employees who are customarily employed for five (5) months or less in a calendar year; (vi) (a) employees who are “highly compensated employees” of the Company or any Participating Corporation (within the meaning of Section 414(q) of the Code), or (b) any employees who are “highly compensated employees” with compensation above a specified level, who is an officer and/or is subject to the disclosure requirements of Section 16(a) of the Exchange Act; (vii) employees who are citizens or residents of a foreign jurisdiction (without regard to whether they are also a citizen of the United States or a resident alien (within the meaning of Section 7701(b)(1)(A) of the Code)) if either (i) such employee’s participation is prohibited under the laws of the jurisdiction governing such employee, or (ii) compliance with the laws of the foreign jurisdiction would violate the requirements of Section 423 of the Code; and (viii) individuals who provide services to the Company or any of its Participating Corporations who are reclassified as common law employees for any reason except for federal income and employment tax purposes. The foregoing notwithstanding, an individual shall not be eligible if his or her participation in this Plan is prohibited by the law of any country that has jurisdiction over him or her, if complying with the laws of the applicable country would cause this Plan to violate Section 423 of the Code, or if he or she is subject to a collective bargaining agreement that does not provide for participation in this Plan. (b) No employee who, together with any other person whose stock would be attributed to such employee pursuant to Section 424(d) of the Code, owns stock or holds options to purchase stock possessing five percent (5%) or more of the total combined voting power or value of all classes of stock of the Company or its Parent or Subsidiary or who, as a result of being granted an option under this Plan with respect to such Offering Period, would own stock or hold options to purchase stock possessing five percent (5%) or more of the total combined voting power or value of all classes of stock of the Company or its Parent or Subsidiary shall be granted an option to purchase Common Stock under this Plan. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the rules of Section 424(d) of the Code shall apply in determining share ownership and the extent to which shares held under outstanding equity awards are to be treated as owned by the employee. 5. OFFERING DATES. (a) Each Offering Period of this Plan may be of up to twenty-seven (27) months duration and shall commence and end at the times designated by the Committee. Each Offering Period shall consist of one or more Purchase Periods during which Contributions made by Participants are accumulated under this Plan. Offering Periods may be consecutive or overlapping. (b) An Offering Period shall commence on such dates as are specified by the Committee, with each such Offering Period also consisting of a six (6)-month Purchase Period, except as otherwise provided by an applicable sub-plan, or on such other date determined by the Committee. The Committee may at any time establish a different duration for an Offering Period or Purchase Period to be effective after the next scheduled Purchase Date, up to a maximum duration of twenty-seven (27) months. 6. PARTICIPATION IN THIS PLAN. (a) Enrollment in Offering Period. An eligible employee determined in accordance with Section 4 may elect to participate in this Plan by submitting an enrollment agreement prior to the commencement of the Offering Period (or such earlier date as the Committee may determine) to which such agreement relates to the Company and/or an authorized third party administrator (the “ Third Party Administrator ”) (including electronically). (b) Continued Enrollment in Offering Periods . Once an employee becomes a Participant in an Offering Period, then such Participant will automatically participate in each subsequent Offering Period commencing immediately following the last day of the prior Offering Period unless the Participant withdraws or is deemed to withdraw from this Plan or terminates further participation in an Offering Period as set forth in Section 11 of this Plan. A Participant who is continuing participation pursuant to the preceding sentence is not required to file or submit electronically any additional enrollment agreement in order to continue participation in this Plan, but participation in any subsequent Offering Period will be governed by this Plan and enrollment agreement and other terms in effect on the Offering Date for such relevant Offering Period. A Participant who has discontinued participation in this Plan will be required to submit an enrollment agreement to the Company and/or the Third Party Administrator (including electronically) prior to the commencement of the Offering Period (or such earlier date as the Committee may determine) in which such Participant wishes to resume participation. 7. GRANT OF OPTION ON ENROLLMENT. Becoming a Participant with respect to an Offering Period will constitute the grant (as of the Offering Date) by the Company to such Participant of an option to purchase on the Purchase Date up to that number of shares of Common Stock determined by a fraction, the numerator of which is the amount accumulated in such Participant’s Contribution account during such Purchase Period and the denominator of which is the lower of (i) eighty-five percent (85%) of the Fair Market Value of a share of Common Stock on the Offering Date (but in no event less than the par value of a share of the Common Stock), or (ii) eighty-five percent (85%) of the Fair Market Value of a share of the Common Stock on the Purchase Date; provided , that , the number of shares of Common Stock subject to any option granted pursuant to this Plan shall not exceed the lesser of (x) the maximum number of shares set by the Committee pursuant to Section 10(b) of this Plan with respect to the applicable Purchase Date, or (y) the maximum number of shares which may be purchased pursuant to Section 10(a) of this Plan with respect to the applicable Purchase Date. 8. PURCHASE PRICE. The Purchase Price per share at which a share of Common Stock will be sold in any Offering Period shall be eighty-five percent (85%) of the lesser of: (a) The Fair Market Value on the Offering Date; or (b) The Fair Market Value on the Purchase Date. 9. PAYMENT OF PURCHASE PRICE; CONTRIBUTION CHANGES; SHARE ISSUANCES. In the event that this Plan has been oversubscribed, all funds not used to purchase shares on the Purchase Date shall be returned to the Participant, without interest (except to the extent required due to local legal requirements outside the United States).
