text: EX-10.2 3 none-ex10_2.htm EX-10.2 EX-10.2 FOURTH AMENDED AND RESTATED DIVIDEND REINVESTMENT AND DIRECT SHARE PURCHASE PLAN This Fourth Amended and Restated Dividend Reinvestment and Direct Share Purchase Plan (the “ Plan ”) has been adopted by ExchangeRight Income Fund (the “ Company ”) pursuant to its Amended and Restated Declaration of Trust (as amended, restated or otherwise modified from time to time, the “ Charter ”). Unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms shall have the same meaning as set forth in the Charter. 1. Administration of the Plan. The Plan shall be administered by the Company as agent for Participants in the Plan. All the costs to administer the Plan shall be paid by the Company. The Company may adopt rules and regulations to facilitate the administration of the Plan, and reserves the right to interpret the provisions of the Plan and any rules and regulations adopted in accordance therewith, in its sole discretion. The determination of any matter with respect to the Plan made by the Company in good faith shall be final and conclusive and binding on the Company and all Participants (defined below). 2. Dividend Reinvestment. As agent for (i) the shareholders (the “ Shareholders ”) of the Company (the “ Shareholders ”) who (A) purchase the Company’s common shares of beneficial interest, $0.01 par value per share, whether designated as of the date hereof or hereinafter designated in the Charter (collectively, the “ Shares ”), pursuant to the Company’s continuous private placement offering of Common Shares that is ongoing as of the date of adoption of this Plan, or (B) purchase Shares pursuant to any future offering of the Company, and who elect to participate in the Plan, and (ii) the holders (“ OP Unitholders ”) of the Class I Common Units, Class A 721 Common Units, Class D Common Units, NLP Common Units, and each series thereof, AC Common Units, and each series thereof, and Class T Common Units of limited partnership interest (collectively, the “ OP Units ”) in ExchangeRight Income Fund Operating Partnership, LP, a Delaware limited partnership and the operating partnership of the Company, who elect to participate in the Plan and make direct Share purchases pursuant to Section 4(b) of this Plan (each, a “ Participant ,” and collectively the “ Participants ”), the Company will apply any such cash dividends and other distributions declared and paid in respect of the Shares or OP Units held by each Participant, as the case may be, and attributable to the class of Shares or OP Units held by such Participant (the “ Distributions ”), including Distributions paid with respect to any full or fractional Shares acquired under the Plan, (x) to the purchase of additional Shares of the same class for Participants who are Shareholders (except with respect to Shareholders of Class ER-I, ER-D, ER-A, and ER-S Common Shares of the Company, which shall have Distributions in respect of such Shares applied to the purchase of additional Class I Common Shares, Class D Common Shares, Class A Common Shares, and Class S Common Shares of beneficial interest, $0.01 par value per share, of the Company, respectively), (y) in the case of Participants who are OP Unitholders of Class I Common Units, Class A 721 Common Units, NLP 20 Common Units, NLP 23 Common Units, NLP 24 Common Units, NLP 25 Common Units, NLP 26 Common Units, NLP 27 Common Units, NLP 47 Common Units, NLP 49 Common Units, NLP 51 Common Units, and NLP 53 Common Units, to the purchase of Class I Common Shares, or (z) in the case of Participants who are OP Unitholders of Class D Common Units, Class T Common Units, AC Common Units, and each series thereof, and each series of NLP Common Units not otherwise specified in clause (y) above, to the purchase of Class D Common Shares. 3. Effective Date. The initial effective date of this Plan, prior to its amendment and restatement, was October 19, 2023 (the “ Effective Date ”), the effective date of the Amended and Restated Plan was May 30, 2024, the effective date of the Second Amended and Restated Plan was June 10, 2025, the effective date of the Third Amended and Restated Plan was March 18, 2026, and the effective date of this Fourth Amended and Restated Plan shall be November 18, 2026. 4. Procedure for Participation. Fourth Amended and Restated Dividend Reinvestment and Direct Share Purchase Plan - 1 - (a) Shareholders. Any Shareholder who has received a copy of the Company’s private placement memorandum provided in connection with the offering of Shares pursuant to the Plan (as amended and/or supplemented from time to time, the “ DRIP Offering Memorandum ”), will be eligible to become a Participant at the Shareholder’s discretion, at any time on or after the Effective Date, by completing an enrollment form and agreement (“ Enrollment Form ”) to reinvest all or part of the Shareholder’s Distributions that are or become payable on Shares held by such Shareholder and returning the Enrollment Form to the Company. If a Shareholder’s Enrollment Form is received prior to the record date for a Distribution, participation in the Plan by the Shareholder will begin with the payment date of the Distribution payable in respect of Shares to which the record date applies after the acceptance of a Shareholder’s Enrollment Form. If a Shareholder’s Enrollment Form is received on or after any record date for a Distribution, participation in the Plan by the Shareholder will begin with the payment date of the Distribution payable in respect of Shares following the next succeeding record date after the acceptance of a Shareholder’s Enrollment Form. Shares for the accounts of Shareholders will be purchased under the Plan on the date that Distributions are paid by the Company in respect of Shares. (b) Direct Share Purchase Option for OP Unitholders. Any OP Unitholder who has received a copy of the DRIP Offering Memorandum will be eligible, at the OP Unitholder’s discretion, to become a Participant and make direct Share purchases from the Company, at any time on or after the Effective Date, by completing an Enrollment Form to apply all or part of the OP Unitholder’s Distributions in respect of the OP Units held by such OP Unitholder to the purchase of Class I Common Shares or Class D Common Shares, as applicable, and returning the Enrollment Form to the Company (“ Direct Share Purchases ”). If an OP Unitholder’s Enrollment Form is received prior to the record date for a Distribution, participation in the Plan by the OP Unitholder will begin with the payment date of the Distribution payable in respect of OP Units to which the record date applies after the acceptance of an OP Unitholder’s Enrollment Form. If an OP Unitholder’s Enrollment Form is received on or after any record date for a Distribution, participation in the Plan by the OP Unitholder will begin with the payment date of the Distribution payable in respect of OP Units following the next succeeding record date after the acceptance of an OP Unitholder’s Enrollment Form. Direct Share Purchases for the accounts of OP Unitholders will be made under the Plan on the date that Distributions are paid by the Operating Partnership in respect of OP Units. 5. Suitability. Each Participant is required to be an “Accredited Investor” as defined in Section 501(a) of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and any other investment suitability standards imposed by the Company and set forth in the DRIP Offering Memorandum. Each Participant is requested to promptly notify the Company in writing if the Participant experiences a material change in his or her financial condition, including the failure to meet the income, net worth and investment concentration standards imposed by such Participant’s state of residence and set forth in the Company’s most recent DRIP Offering Memorandum. 6. Purchase of Shares. Participants will acquire Shares from the Company (including Shares purchased by the Company for the Plan in a secondary market (if available) or on a stock exchange (if listed)) under the Plan (the “ Plan Shares ”) at a price equal to 99% of the net asset value per Share (calculated quarterly) in effect as of the most recent record date for a Distribution, as determined by the Trustee. No upfront selling commissions will be payable with respect to Shares purchased pursuant to the Plan, and the Plan Shares shall not be subject to ongoing shareholder servicing fees. Participants in the Plan may purchase fractional Shares so that 100% of the Distributions will be used to acquire Plan Shares. However, a Participant will not be able to acquire Plan Shares and such Participant’s participation in the Plan will be terminated to the extent that a reinvestment of such Participant’s Distributions in Shares or Direct Share Purchases, as the case may be, would cause the percentage ownership or other limitations contained in the Charter to be violated. 7. Taxes. THE REINVESTMENT OF DISTRIBUTIONS DOES NOT RELIEVE A PARTICIPANT OF ANY INCOME TAX LIABILITY THAT MAY BE PAYABLE ON THE DISTRIBUTIONS. INFORMATION REGARDING POTENTIAL INCOME TAX LIABILITY OF PARTICIPANTS MAY BE FOUND IN THE DRIP OFFERING MEMORANDUM. Fourth Amended and Restated Dividend Reinvestment and Direct Share Purchase Plan - 2 - 8. Book-Entry Form. The ownership of the Shares purchased through the Plan will be in book-entry form unless and until the Company issues certificates for its outstanding Shares. 9. Reports. On a quarterly basis, the Company shall provide each Participant a statement of account describing, as to such Participant: (i) the Distributions reinvested or Direct Share Purchases made, as the case may be, during the quarter; (ii) the number and class of Shares purchased pursuant to the Plan during the quarter; (iii) the per Share purchase price for such Shares; and (iv) the total number of Shares purchased on behalf of the Participant under the Plan. In addition, Participants will receive copies of other communications sent to holders of Shares or OP Units, including quarterly investor reports, notices and proxy statements in connection with meetings of the Company’s shareholders, and any tax related information for reporting Distributions paid. 10. Termination by Participant. A Participant may terminate participation in the Plan with respect to all or a portion of the Shares or OP Units held by such Participant at any time by delivering written notice to ExchangeRight Income Fund Trustee, LLC, as the trustee of the Company (the “ Trustee ”). If the request to terminate participation is received prior to a Distribution record date set by the Trustee for determining Shareholders or OP Unitholders of record entitled to receive a Distribution, the request will be processed on the day following receipt of the termination request by the Trustee. If the request to terminate participation is received by the Trustee within two business days prior to a Distribution record date, the Trustee, in its sole discretion, may either pay the Distribution to the Participant in cash or reinvest the Distribution in or make a Direct Share Purchase of Plan Shares for the Participant’s account. Any transfer of Shares or OP Units, as the case may be, by a Participant to a non-Participant will terminate participation in the Plan with respect to the transferred Shares or OP Units. If a Participant requests that the Company repurchase all or any portion of the Participant’s Shares, or that the Operating Partnership repurchase all or any portion of the Participant’s OP Units, as the case may be, the Participant’s participation in the Plan with respect to the Participant’s Shares or OP Units, as the case may be, for which repurchase was requested but that were not repurchased will be terminated. Upon termination of Plan participation for any reason, future Distributions will be distributed to the Shareholder or OP Unitholder, as the case may be, in cash. 11. Amendment, Suspension or Termination by the Company. The Trustee may amend any aspect of the Plan; provided that the Plan cannot be amended to eliminate a Participant’s right to terminate participation in the Plan and that notice of any material amendment must be provided to Participants at least 10 calendar days prior to the effective date of that amendment. The Trustee may suspend or terminate the Plan for any reason upon 10 business days’ written notice to the Participants. 12. Liability of the Company. The Company and the Trustee will not be liable in administering the Plan for any act done in good faith or required by applicable law or for any good faith omission to act including, without limitation, any claim of liability arising out of failure to terminate a Participant’s account upon his or her death, with respect to the prices at which Shares are purchased and/or the times when those purchases are made or with respect to any fluctuation in the value before or after purchase. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing contained in the Plan limits the Company’s liability with respect to violations of applicable federal or state securities laws. The Company and the Trustee will be entitled to rely on completed Enrollment Forms and the proof of suitability and due authority to participate in the Plan, without further responsibility of investigation or inquiry. text: EX-10.1 3 ex10_1.htm ESCROW RELEASE AND TERMINATION AGREEMENT, DATED NOVEMBER 19, 2026 Exhibit 10.1 ESCROW RELEASE AND TERMINATION AGREEMENT This ESCROW RELEASE AND TERMINATION AGREEMENT (this “Release Agreement”) is made as of November 19, 2026, the date on which the First Amendment (as defined below) becomes effective (the “Release Date”) by and among CLEARTRUST, LLC, a Florida limited liability company (the “Escrow Agent”); STEWARDS, INC., a Nevada corporation (“Party A”); and ENVY DEVELOPMENT PB, LLC, a Florida limited liability company, and THE MYELIN GROUP, LLC, a Florida limited liability company (together, “Party B”; each of them a “Seller”). The Escrow Agent, Party A and Party B are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” RECITALS A. The Parties are parties to that certain Escrow Agreement made as of September 23, 2026 (the “Escrow Agreement”), under which the Escrow Agent holds 7,000,000 shares of common stock of Party A (the “Escrow Shares”), registered in the names of the Sellers and coded with a stop transfer, in the amounts shown on Annex 1. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Release Agreement have the meanings given in the Escrow Agreement. B. The Escrow Shares were deposited under the Membership Interests Purchase and Sale Agreement dated as of September 21, 2026 (the “Purchase Agreement”) among Party A, SRC Envy Holdco LLC, the Sellers and the other parties to it. Section 5 of Exhibit A to the Escrow Agreement provides for release of the Escrow Shares on joint written instructions of Party A and Party B given in accordance with Section 2.2.2(b) of the Purchase Agreement, on the fifth day of a month, and for release to Party A of any Escrow Shares remaining in escrow on April 5, 2027. C. Party A and the Sellers have entered into a First Amendment to the Purchase Agreement dated as of November 13, 2026 (the “First Amendment”), under which the Escrow Shares are to be delivered to Party A for cancellation in exchange for shares of Party A’s Series D Convertible Preferred Stock, in full and final satisfaction of the consideration they represent, and the Escrow Agreement is to terminate. D. The Parties wish to give the Escrow Agent joint instructions to deliver the Escrow Shares to Party A for cancellation, to confirm the conditions to that delivery, and to terminate the Escrow Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Release Agreement and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Joint Instruction. Party A and Party B jointly and irrevocably instruct the Escrow Agent to deliver the Escrow Shares to Party A for cancellation, on the Release Date or, if later, on the Escrow Agent’s receipt of this Release Agreement signed by all Parties and satisfaction of Section 3 (the “Release Time”), in book-entry form, as follows: (a) the 6,766,900 shares registered in the name of Envy Development PB, LLC; and (b) the 233,100 shares registered in the name of The Myelin Group, LLC, in each case for cancellation by Party A’s transfer agent concurrently with the issuance to that Seller of an equal number of shares of Party A’s Series D Convertible Preferred Stock under the First Amendment. The Escrow Shares registered in a Seller’s name shall not be cancelled unless the Series D Convertible Preferred Stock deliverable to that Seller is issued as required herein. The stop-transfer coding applied under Section 2.2 of the Escrow Agreement remains in place until cancellation, and no Escrow Share shall be released to any Seller. 2. Amendment of Instructions. The Instructions in Section 5 of Exhibit A to the Escrow Agreement are amended, as permitted by Section 1.1 of the Escrow Agreement and as agreed by all Parties for purposes of Section 5.2 of the Escrow Agreement, so that: (a) the release described in Section 1 occurs at the Release Time and not on the fifth day of any later month; (b) the provision that Escrow Shares remaining in escrow on April 5, 2027 are released to Party A no longer applies; and (c) all Escrow Shares are to be delivered to Party A for cancellation as provided in Section 1, and none to Party B. This Release Agreement is the signed Instructions required by Section 2.2 of the Escrow Agreement and the joint written instruction contemplated by Exhibit A to it. 3. Conditions to Release. The Escrow Agent’s obligation to release the Escrow Shares is subject only to the following, as required by Section 3.1(a) of the Escrow Agreement: (a) the Parties, along with their respective principals, owners and managing members, have cleared the OFAC scan performed by the Escrow Agent at the time it receives this Release Agreement; (b) the Escrow Agent Fees of $6,000.00 and any other invoiced fees and Expenses have been paid in full; and (c) the Escrow Agent and each Seller have received written confirmation from Party A’s transfer agent that the shares of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock deliverable to each Seller under the First Amendment have been issued, or will be issued at the Release Time, in book-entry form in that Seller’s name. Party A confirms that it has paid, or will pay at or before the Release Time, those fees and Expenses, and the Escrow Agent shall confirm in writing to the Parties whether each condition has been met. If a Party or one of its principals, owners or managing members does not clear the OFAC scan, Section 3.1(a) of the Escrow Agreement applies to the Escrow Shares allocated to that Party. If the conditions in this Section 3 have not been met by November 30, 2026, the instruction in Section 1 lapses unless Party A and Party B extend it in writing, and the Escrow Shares remain in escrow under the Escrow Agreement. 4. Confirmations by the Escrow Agent. The Escrow Agent confirms that, as of the Release Date: (a) it holds all 7,000,000 Escrow Shares, registered as shown on Annex 1; (b) it has not received any Court Order, judicial or administrative order, writ, levy, attachment, garnishment, injunction or stay affecting the Escrow Shares, and has not been notified of any dispute under Section 3.3 or Section 4.2 of the Escrow Agreement; (c) it has not released, delivered or transferred any Escrow Shares; and (d) it has not received any competing instruction from any Party. 5. Representations of the Sellers and Party A. Each Seller represents to the other Parties that, as to the Escrow Shares registered in its name: (a) it has full power and authority to sign and perform this Release Agreement; and (b) it has not sold, pledged, transferred or encumbered any right in the Escrow Shares, other than under the Escrow Agreement and the Purchase Agreement. Party A represents that it has full power and authority to sign and perform this Release Agreement and that its board of directors (including its Audit Committee) has approved the First Amendment. Party A further represents that the certificate of designation for its Series D Convertible Preferred Stock has been filed and is effective, and that the shares of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock to be issued to each Seller, when issued, will be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable, and free of any lien or encumbrance created by Party A. 6. Termination. Effective at the Release Time, and on release of all of the Escrow Shares, the Escrow Agreement terminates under Section 5.9 of the Escrow Agreement, and the Parties modify it as necessary to give effect to that termination, as permitted by Section 5.2. The following survive termination: Article IV of the Escrow Agreement (including the indemnity in Article IV(c) and the tax provision in Article IV(i)); the Escrow Agent’s obligation under Article IV(m) to deliver its records after payment of all outstanding invoices; and any obligation to pay fees and Expenses properly incurred before the Release Time. After the Release Time no Party has any further obligation to another under the Escrow Agreement except as stated in this Section 6. Nothing in this Release Agreement limits any right or obligation of Party A or the Sellers under the Purchase Agreement or the First Amendment, including Party A’s obligation to issue the Series D Convertible Preferred Stock. 7. Release of the Escrow Agent. At the Release Time, and subject to the survival provisions in Section 6, Party A and each Seller releases the Escrow Agent from all claims arising from its holding and release of the Escrow Shares in accordance with the Escrow Agreement and this Release Agreement, except for claims arising from the Escrow Agent’s willful misconduct, fraud or gross negligence, as stated in Article IV(c) of the Escrow Agreement. 8. Transfer Agent Capacity. If the Escrow Agent or an affiliate also acts as transfer agent for Party A, nothing in this Release Agreement changes or waives its obligations or authority under that engagement. Nothing in this Release Agreement authorizes any transfer, deposit or legend removal of Common Stock. Any such action is governed by Party A’s separate transfer agent instruction letter, which Party A is delivering to the Escrow Agent at the Release Time. 9. General. This Release Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, and Sections 5.7 and 5.8 of the Escrow Agreement apply to it as if set out in full. It may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original. It may be changed only in writing signed by all Parties. Together with the Escrow Agreement as modified by it, it is the entire agreement of the Parties on its subject. If this Release Agreement conflicts with the Escrow Agreement, this Release Agreement controls. Each Party shall sign and deliver any further document reasonably requested to carry out this Release Agreement. [SIGNATURES APPEAR ON FOLLOWING PAGE] 2 ESCROW RELEASE AND TERMINATION AGREEMENT IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have signed this Escrow Release and Termination Agreement as of the Release Date. Class: Common Stock Agreed contractual value: $21,000,000 4

title: Arrive AI Inc.
text: EX-10.1 3 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 THE EXCHANGE CONTEMPLATED HEREIN IS INTENDED TO COMPORT WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 3(a)(9) OF THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED. Exchange Agreement This Exchange Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is entered into as of November 18, 2026 by and between Arrive AI Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ Company ”), and Streeterville Capital, LLC, a Utah limited liability company (“ Investor ”). A. Pursuant to that certain Securities Purchase Agreement dated March 21, 2025 between Company and Investor (the “ Purchase Agreement ”), Company issued to Investor the following Pre-Paid Purchases that are still outstanding: (i) that certain Pre-Paid Purchase #2 dated August 11, 2025 in the original principal amount of $4,320,000.00 (“ PPP #2 ”); (ii) that certain Pre-Paid Purchase #3 dated December 3, 2025 in the original principal amount of $3,240,000.00 (“ PPP #3 ”); and (iii) that certain Pre-Paid Purchase #5 dated August 14, 2026 in the original principal amount of $108,000.00 (“ PPP #5 ”, and together with PPP #2 and PPP #3, the “ Exchanged PPPs ”). B. Company and Investor further desire to exchange (the “ Exchange ”) the Exchanged PPPs for 3,962 shares of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock with a stated value of $1,050 per share (the “ Exchange Shares ”). C. This Agreement, the Certificate of Designation (as defined below), the Officer’s Certificate (as defined below), and any other documents, agreements, or instruments entered into or delivered in connection with this Agreement, or any amendments to any of the foregoing, are collectively referred to as the “ Exchange Documents ”. D. Pursuant to the terms and conditions hereof, Investor and Company agree to exchange the Exchanged PPPs for the Exchange Shares. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the mutual promises herein made, and in consideration of the representations, warranties and covenants herein contained, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Issuance of Exchange Shares . At Closing, Investor will surrender the Exchanged PPPs to Company and Company will issue to Investor the Exchange Shares. In conjunction therewith, Company hereby confirms that the Exchanged PPPs represent Company’s unconditional obligation to pay the outstanding balance thereof pursuant to the terms of the Exchanged PPPs. Company and Investor agree that upon surrender, the Exchanged PPPs will be cancelled and the remaining amount owed to Investor pursuant to the Exchanged PPPs will hereafter be evidenced solely by the Exchange Shares. 2. Closing Date; Deliveries . The closing of the transaction contemplated hereby (the “ Closing ”) along with the Exchange Documents shall occur on the date that is mutually agreed to by Company and Investor following satisfaction of the Closing Conditions (the “ Closing Date ”) by means of the exchange of electronic signatures, but shall be deemed to have occurred at the offices of Capital Law Partners PLLC in Lehi, Utah. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall the Closing Date occur later than November 20, 2026 (the “ Outside Date ”), unless otherwise agreed in writing by Company and Investor. If the Closing has not occurred on or before the Outside Date, this Agreement shall automatically terminate and be of no further force or effect, and the Exchanged PPPs shall remain outstanding in accordance with their existing terms. The obligation of the parties to complete the Exchange is subject to satisfaction (or written waiver by Investor), on or before the Closing Date, of each of the following conditions (the “ Closing Conditions ”): 2.1. Company shall have filed the Certificate of Designation of Preferences and Rights of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A (the “ Certificate of Designation ”) with the State of Nevada and received confirmation from the State of Nevada that such Certificate of Designation has been accepted and approved. 2.2. Company shall have issued the Exchange Shares to Investor, which issuance will not be evidenced by the physical delivery of certificated shares, but instead will be properly reflected on the books and records of Company. 2.3. Company shall have delivered to Investor a fully executed Officer’s Certificate substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit B (the “ Officer’s Certificate ”) evidencing the Company’s approval of the Exchange and the Exchange Documents. 2.4. Mutual delivery of all Exchange Documents, including without limitation this Agreement. 2.5. Company’s common stock is trading on Nasdaq on the Closing Date. 3. Holding Period . Company represents, warrants and agrees that for the purposes of Rule 144 (“ Rule 144 ”) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “ Securities Act ”), the holding period of the Exchange Shares will include the holding period of the Exchanged PPPs. Company agrees not to take a position contrary to this Section 3 in any document, statement, setting, or situation. The Exchange Shares are being issued in substitution of and exchange for and not in satisfaction of the Exchanged PPPs. The Exchange Shares shall not constitute a novation or satisfaction and accord of the Exchanged PPPs. Company acknowledges and understands that the representations and agreements of Company in this Section 3 are a material inducement to Investor’s decision to consummate the transactions contemplated herein. 4. Investor’s Representations, Warranties and Agreements . In order to induce Company to enter into this Agreement, Investor, for itself, and for its affiliates, successors and assigns, hereby acknowledges, represents, warrants and agrees as follows: (a) Investor has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to incur and perform all obligations and covenants contained herein, all of which have been duly authorized by all proper and necessary action, (b) no consent, approval, filing or registration with or notice to any governmental authority is required as a condition to the validity of this Agreement or the performance of any of the obligations of Investor hereunder, (c) no consideration or commission has been paid or given directly or indirectly by Investor to Company or any broker in connection with the Exchange, and (d) Investor has taken no action which would give rise to any claim by any person for a brokerage commission, placement agent or finder’s fee or other similar payment by Company related to this Agreement. 5. Company’s Representations, Warranties and Agreements . In order to induce Investor to enter into this Agreement, Company, for itself, and for its affiliates, successors and assigns, hereby acknowledges, represents, warrants and agrees as follows: (a) Company has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to incur and perform all obligations and covenants contained herein, all of which have been duly authorized by all proper and necessary action, (b) except as provided herein, no consent, approval, filing or registration with or notice to any governmental authority is required as a condition to the validity of this Agreement or the performance of any of the obligations of Company hereunder, (c) no Event of Default (as defined in the Exchanged PPPs) has occurred under the Exchanged PPPs; provided, however, that notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, to the extent any Event of Default has occurred or may hereafter occur, such Event of Default has not been, and is not hereby, waived by Investor, (d) the issuance of the Exchange Shares is duly authorized by all necessary corporate action, (e) Company has not received any consideration in any form whatsoever for entering into this Agreement, other than the surrender of the Exchanged PPPs, (f) Company has taken no action which would give rise to any claim by any person for a brokerage commission, placement agent or finder’s fee or other similar payment by Company related to this Agreement, and (g) Company’s Board of Directors has duly adopted a resolution authorizing this Agreement and the other Exchange Documents and ratifying their terms, as indicated by the Officer’s Certificate. 2 6. Application of Purchase Agreement . The governing law, venue, jury waiver and arbitration provisions of the Purchase Agreement are incorporated herein by reference and will apply to this Agreement, the Certificate of Designation and the Exchange Shares as if set forth herein in full. 7. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered via electronic signature (including pdf or any electronic signature complying with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000, e.g., www.docusign.com) and any counterpart so delivered shall be deemed to have been duly and validly delivered and be valid and effective for all purposes. 8. Attorneys’ Fees . In the event of any arbitration or action at law or in equity to enforce or interpret the terms of this Agreement, the parties agree that the prevailing party shall be entitled to an additional award of the full amount of the attorneys’ fees and expenses paid by such prevailing party in connection with the arbitration, litigation and/or dispute without reduction or apportionment based upon the individual claims or defenses giving rise to the fees and expenses. The “prevailing party” shall be the party in whose favor a judgment is entered, regardless of whether judgment is entered on all claims asserted by such party and regardless of the amount of the judgment; or where, due to the assertion of counterclaims, judgments are entered in favor of and against both parties, then the arbitrator shall determine the “prevailing party” by taking into account the relative dollar amounts of the judgments or, if the judgments involve nonmonetary relief, the relative importance and value of such relief. Nothing herein shall restrict or impair an arbitrator’s or a court’s power to award reasonable fees and expenses for frivolous or bad faith pleading. 9. No Reliance . Company acknowledges and agrees that neither Investor nor any of its officers, directors, members, managers, equity holders, representatives or agents has made any representations or warranties to Company or any of its agents, representatives, officers, directors, or employees except as expressly set forth in this Agreement and the Exchange Documents and, in making its decision to enter into the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, Company is not relying on any representation, warranty, covenant or promise of Investor or its officers, directors, members, managers, equity holders, agents or representatives other than as set forth in this Agreement. 10. Severability . If any part of this Agreement is construed to be in violation of any law, such part shall be modified to achieve the objective of the parties to the fullest extent permitted and the balance of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect. 11. Entire Agreement . This Agreement, together with the Exchange Documents and the Transaction Documents, and all other documents referred to herein, supersedes all other prior oral or written agreements among Company, Investor, its affiliates and persons acting on its behalf with respect to the matters discussed herein, and this Agreement and the instruments referenced herein contain the entire understanding of the parties with respect to the matters covered herein and therein and, except as specifically set forth herein or therein, neither Investor nor Company makes any representation, warranty, covenant or undertaking with respect to such matters. 3 12. Amendments . This Agreement may be amended, modified, or supplemented only by written agreement of the parties. No provision of this Agreement may be waived except in writing signed by the party against whom such waiver is sought to be enforced. 13. Successors and Assigns . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and assigns. This Agreement or any of the severable rights and obligations inuring to the benefit of or to be performed by Investor hereunder may be assigned by Investor to a third party, including its financing sources, in whole or in part. Company may not assign this Agreement or any of its obligations herein without the prior written consent of Investor. 14. Continuing Enforceability; Conflict Between Documents . Except as otherwise modified by this Agreement, each of the Exchange Documents and Transaction Documents shall remain in full force and effect, enforceable in accordance with all of its original terms and provisions, and the Exchange Shares shall be in full force and effect from its date of issuance in accordance with its terms. This Agreement shall not be effective or binding unless and until it is fully executed and delivered by Investor and Company. If there is any conflict between the terms of this Agreement, on the one hand, and the Exchange Shares or any other Exchange Document or Transaction Document, on the other hand, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail. 15. Time of Essence . Time is of the essence with respect to each and every provision of this Agreement. 16. Notices . Unless otherwise specifically provided for herein, all notices, demands or requests required or permitted under this Agreement to be given to Company or Investor shall be given as set forth in the “Notices” section of the Purchase Agreement. 17. Further Assurances . Each party shall do and perform or cause to be done and performed, all such further acts and things, and shall execute and deliver all such other agreements, certificates, instruments and documents, as the other party may reasonably request in order to carry out the intent and accomplish the purposes of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. [Remainder of the page intentionally left blank; signature page to follow] 4 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned have executed this Agreement as of the date first set forth above. INVESTOR: Streeterville Capital, LLC By: /s/ John Fife John Fife, President COMPANY: Arrive AI Inc. By: /s/ Daniel O’Toole Daniel O’Toole, Chief Executive Officer ATTACHMENTS: Exhibit A Certificate of Designation Exhibit B Officer’s Certificate [Signature Page to Exchange Agreement] 5

text: EX-10.2 4 ex10-2.htm EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 STREETERVILLE CAPITAL, LLC November 18, 2026 Arrive AI Inc. Attn: Daniel O’Toole dan@arriveai.com Re: Conditional Consent to Use of ATM Dear Dan: This letter agreement (this “ Letter Agreement ”) is entered into by and between Streeterville Capital, LLC, a Utah limited liability company (“ Investor ”), and Arrive AI Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ Company ”), in connection with Company’s Certificate of Designation of Preferences and Rights of Convertible Series A Preferred Stock (the “ Series A Certificate ”). Reference is also made to that certain Exchange Agreement by and between Investor and Company of even date herewith (the “ Exchange Agreement ”). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein will have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Series A Certificate. Investor and Company hereby agree as follows: 1. Conditional Consent to Use of ATM . (a) Investor hereby grants its consent for Company to sell Common Shares under its ATM, notwithstanding Section 11(e) of the Series A Certificate, subject to the terms of this Section 1. The foregoing consent may be revoked by Investor at any time by delivering written notice of such to Company. (b) For each week that Company sells Common Shares under its ATM, Company shall pay Investor, by wire transfer of immediately available funds, an amount equal to thirty-three percent (33%) of the net proceeds from all sales settled during that week (each, a “ Sweep Payment ”). (c) Sweep Payments will automatically be applied to the redemption of shares of Series A Stock held by Investor, at the amount of one hundred percent (100%) of the Stated Value set forth in the Series A Certificate; and (d) Upon Investor’s request, if any sales were made pursuant to the ATM during the preceding week, Company shall provide Investor with a report detailing the aggregate number of shares sold and gross proceeds received from such sales during such week. (e) Any failure to make a Sweep Payment when due shall be considered an event of default under the Series A Certificate. (f) This consent is limited to the matters expressly set forth herein. It does not waive any other provision of any other agreement between the parties or any default thereunder. 2. Conflict . In the event of a conflict between the terms and conditions contained in this Letter Agreement and those contained in any other agreement or document related to the Exchange Agreement or the Series A Certificate, the terms and conditions contained herein shall control. 3. Incorporation of Purchase Agreement Provisions . Section 6 of the Exchange Agreement incorporating the provisions of the Purchase Agreement (as defined in the Exchange Agreement) shall also apply to this Letter Agreement, mutatis mutandis, as if fully set forth herein. 4. Assignment; Binding upon Successors and Assigns . Company may not assign any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of Investor. Investor may assign its rights and obligations hereunder, in whole or in part, without the consent of Company. This Letter Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns. 5. Amendment and Waivers . Any term or provision of this Letter Agreement may be amended and the observance of any term of this Letter Agreement may be waived (either generally or in a particular instance and either retroactively or prospectively) only by a writing signed by the parties hereto. The waiver by either party of any breach hereof or default in the performance hereof will not be deemed to constitute a waiver of any other default or any succeeding breach or default. 6. Entire Agreement . This Letter Agreement contains the entire understanding between the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes any prior understandings, agreements or representations, written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof, other than the other Exchange Documents (as defined in the Exchange Agreement), which remain in full force and effect and are hereby ratified and confirmed. Except as expressly set forth herein, nothing in this Letter Agreement shall be deemed a waiver or modification of any right or remedy of Investor under the Exchange Documents, all of which are expressly reserved. 7. Counterparts . This Letter Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which when executed and delivered shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute the same agreement. This Letter Agreement may be executed by electronic signature, which shall be considered legally binding for all purposes. 8. Further Assurances . Each party to this Letter Agreement agrees to perform any further acts and execute and deliver any documents that may be reasonably necessary to carry out the provisions of this Letter Agreement. 9. Company Representations . Company represents and warrants to Investor that it has all requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Letter Agreement, and this Letter Agreement has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by Company and constitutes its valid and binding obligation, enforceable against Company in accordance with its terms. [Remainder of page intentionally left blank; signature page to follow] 2 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, Investor and Company have duly executed and delivered this Letter Agreement to be effective as of the date first set forth above. INVESTOR: STREETERVILLE CAPITAL, LLC By: /s/ John Fife John Fife, President ACCEPTED AND AGREED : COMPANY: ARRIVE AI INC. By: /s/ Daniel O’Toole Daniel O’Toole, Chief Executive Officer [Signature Page to Letter Agreement]

text: EX-10.1 2 tm2630318d1_ex10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 November 11, 2026 YA II PN, Ltd. 1012 Springfield Avenue Mountainside, NJ 07092 Attention: Michael Rosselli, Partner Email: mrosselli@yorkvilleadvisors.com Re: Repayment of Pre-Paid Advance Obligation and Participation in ConnectM’s Public Offering Ladies and Gentlemen: This letter agreement (this “Letter”) is between ConnectM Technology Solutions, Inc. (the “Company”) and YA II PN, Ltd. (“Yorkville”). It supplements the Settlement and Termination Agreement between the Company and Yorkville dated December 29, 2025 (the “Settlement Agreement”) with respect to the repayment of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation under the Standby Equity Purchase Agreement between the Company and Yorkville dated December 17, 2024 (the “SEPA”) and the Promissory Note issued by the Company to Yorkville on December 17, 2024 pursuant to the SEPA evidencing the Pre-Paid Advance (the “Note”), in connection with the IPO. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Letter have the meanings given in the Settlement Agreement. “Uplisting” means the listing of the Company’s common stock on the NYSE American in connection with the IPO. For purposes of the definition of “IPO” in the Settlement Agreement, the parties agree that the NYSE American is a mutually agreed national securities exchange. 1. Payoff Amount . “Payoff Amount” means, as of any date, the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation on that date, consisting of (a) unpaid principal, plus (b) accrued and unpaid interest through that date, calculated on the basis of actual days elapsed over a 365-day year, plus (c) any applicable redemption or prepayment premium or fees. No later than two business days before the expected IPO closing date, Yorkville will deliver the payoff letter contemplated by Section 4.3 of the Settlement Agreement, setting forth the Payoff Amount as of the IPO closing date, the daily interest amount after that date and wire instructions. The parties acknowledge and agree that as of November 11, 2026, the amount of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation is as follows: Principal Balance: $ 600,000 Accrued and Unpaid Interest: $ 56,219 Total: $ 656,219 Interest accruing per day (after 11/11/26): $296 2. Payment of the remaining Payoff Amount . Within three business days after the closing of the IPO, the Company will pay Yorkville the total Payoff Amount, calculated as of the date of payment, including interest accrued through the date of payment (the “Final Payment”) as follows: (a) by the issuance of shares in the IPO pursuant to the Participation Payment (as set forth in Section 3 below), if any, and (b) an amount in cash equal to the difference between the Final Payment and the Participation Payment by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account set forth on Exhibit A hereto. ConnectM Technology Solutions, Inc | 2 Mount Royal Ave Ste 550, Marlborough, MA 01752 | 617.395.1333 | www.connectm.com The parties agree that the payment of the Final Payment, made in accordance with this Letter, satisfy the payment timing in Section 4.3 and the repayment condition in Section 5.3(a) of the Settlement Agreement. 3. Participation in the IPO . In the event that the parties wish to satisfy the payment of a portion of the Final Payment by participation in the IPO, then the Company may allocate up to $250,000 of the securities offered in the IPO at the public offering price, which shall be paid for by Yorkville by a reduction of an equal amount of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation (such amount to be paid in accordance with this Section 2, the “Participation Payment”). This indication of interest is not binding. No securities may be sold, and no offer to buy may be accepted, before the registration statement for the IPO is declared effective, and the underwriters may allocate fewer or no securities to Yorkville. The Company’s obligations under Sections 1 does not depend on whether Yorkville purchases securities in the IPO, and Yorkville’s indication of interest does not depend on those payments. 4. Maturity Date . The parties hereby agree that the Maturity Date of the Note shall be extended to January 15, 2027. 5. Ratification of Note; Binding Effect . The Note is in all respects ratified and confirmed and all the terms, conditions and provisions thereof shall remain in full force and effect and the Company hereby acknowledges and agrees that it is indebted to Yorkville under the Note in the amounts set forth herein. 6. Waiver of Claim . The Company hereby acknowledges and agrees that neither it nor its subsidiaries, agents, attorneys, shareholders, advisors, officers, directors, employees, affiliates, predecessors, successors, and assigns (collectively, as the “ Company Parties ”) has any offsets, defenses, claims, or counterclaims against Yorkville or its investment manager, or their respective agents, attorneys, shareholders, managers, members, advisors, officers, directors, employees, affiliates, partners, predecessors, successors, and assigns (collectively, as the “ Released Parties ”), with respect to the Note, the SEPA, the Settlement Agreement, the transactions set forth or otherwise contemplated in this Agreement, or otherwise, and that if any Company Party now has, or ever did have, any offsets, defenses, claims, or counterclaims against any of the Released Parties, whether known or unknown, at law or in equity, from the beginning of the world through this date and through the time of execution of this Agreement, all of them are hereby expressly WAIVED, and each Company Party hereby RELEASES each of the Released Parties therefrom. 7. Settlement Agreement otherwise unchanged . Except as expressly set forth in this Letter, the Settlement Agreement remains in full force and effect, including the termination of the SEPA under Section 5, the Termination Fee Shares under Section 5.2 and the right of first refusal under Section 6. This letter agreement shall satisfy the obligations of the Investor to deliver to the Company a Payoff Letter under the Settlement Agreement. 8. Miscellaneous . This Letter is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and Section 9.3 of the Settlement Agreement (jurisdiction and waiver of jury trial) applies to it. It may be signed in counterparts and by DocuSign or another electronic signature, each of which will be treated as an original. Please confirm Yorkville’s agreement by signing below. Very truly yours, CONNECTM TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS, INC. text: EX-10.2 3 ea031289701ex10-2.htm SECOND AMENDMENT TO CREDIT AGREEMENT, DATED NOVEMBER 19, 2026, AMONG MACH NATURAL RESOURCES LP, THE OTHER CREDIT PARTIES PARTY THERETO, THE LENDERS AND ISSUING BANKS PARTY THERETO AND TRUIST BANK, AS ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT AND COLLATERAL AGENT Exhibit 10.2 Execution Version Second Amendment To Credit Agreement This Second Amendment to Credit Agreement (this “ Second Amendment ”) is dated as of November 19, 2026, by and among Mach Natural Resources LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the “ Borrower ”), the other Credit Parties party hereto, the Issuing Banks party hereto, the Lenders party hereto, and Truist Bank, as administrative agent and collateral agent for the Lenders (in such capacity, together with its successors in such capacity, the “ Administrative Agent ”). Recitals A. The Borrower, the Administrative Agent and the Lenders are parties to that certain Credit Agreement dated as of February 27, 2025 (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified prior to the date hereof, the “ Credit Agreement ”), pursuant to which the Lenders have made certain credit available to and on behalf of the Borrower. B. The Borrower has advised the Administrative Agent that it desires to enter into (i) that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of the date hereof (as amended, restated, amended and restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “ Second Lien Credit Agreement ”), by and among the Borrower, Sixth Street Lending Partners, as administrative agent and collateral agent (in such capacities, together with its successors in such capacities, the “ Second Lien Administrative Agent ”), and the lenders party thereto from time to time (the “ Second Lien Lenders ”), and (ii) the other Second Lien Credit Documents (as defined in Annex A hereto) dated as of the date hereof, including the Second Lien Intercreditor Agreement (as defined in Annex A hereto). Pursuant to the Second Lien Credit Agreement, the Second Lien Lenders have agreed to make term loans (the “ Second Lien Term Loans ”) in an aggregate principal amount equal to $385,000,000 to the Borrower upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein, the proceeds of which will be used (together with proceeds of the Revolving Loans and cash on hand) to repay all outstanding Term Loans and pay fees and expenses relating thereto. C. The Borrower has requested that the Lenders party hereto, constituting at least the Majority Lenders (in accordance with Section 13.1 of the Credit Agreement), and the Administrative Agent enter into this Second Amendment to, among other things, (i) expressly permit the entry into the Second Lien Credit Agreement and the other Second Lien Credit Documents by each Credit Party party thereto and the consummation of the transactions contemplated thereunder and (ii) amend certain other terms of the Credit Agreement, in each case, as set forth herein and subject to the conditions set forth herein. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the mutual covenants herein contained, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: Section 1. Defined Terms . Each capitalized term used herein but not otherwise defined herein (including in the preliminary paragraph and the recitals hereof) has the meaning given such term in the Credit Agreement, as amended by that certain First Amendment to Credit Agreement, dated as of September 12, 2025, and as further amended by this Second Amendment. Unless otherwise indicated, all section references in this Second Amendment refer to sections of the Credit Agreement. Section 2. Amendments to Credit Agreement . In reliance on the representations, warranties, covenants and agreements contained in this Second Amendment, and subject to the satisfaction of the conditions precedent set forth in Section 3 hereof, in each case, effective as of the Second Amendment Effective Date (as hereinafter defined): 2.1 Credit Agreement . The Credit Agreement (other than the signature pages, Exhibits and Schedules thereto) is hereby amended and restated in the form as set forth as Annex A hereto. 2.2 Replacement of Schedule 8.17 to the Credit Agreement . Schedule 8.17 to the Credit Agreement is hereby replaced in its entirety in the form attached as Schedule 8.17 hereto, and Schedule 8.17 hereto shall be deemed to be attached as Schedule 8.17 to the Credit Agreement. 2.3 Repayment of Term Loans; Acknowledgment of the Administrative Agent . (a) Repayment. On the Second Amendment Effective Date and substantially concurrently with the funding of the term loans under the Second Lien Credit Agreement, the Borrower shall apply the proceeds thereof, together with the proceeds of Revolving Loans made on such date and cash on hand, to pay in full in cash to the Administrative Agent, for the account of the Term Lenders, all Term Loans (including all Initial Term Loans) outstanding immediately prior to the effectiveness of this Second Amendment, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon, all fees, and all other amounts then due and payable in respect of the Term Loans under the Credit Agreement and the other Credit Documents (other than contingent indemnification and expense reimbursement obligations for which no claim or demand has been made) (collectively, and as such amount shall be set forth in a payoff statement prepared by the Administrative Agent and delivered to the Borrower prior to the Second Amendment Effective Date, the “ Term Loan Payoff Amount ”). (b) Acknowledgment . The Administrative Agent, for itself and on behalf of each Lender (including each Term Lender), acknowledges and agrees that, effective upon the Administrative Agent’s receipt of the Term Loan Payoff Amount (such time, the “ Term Loan Payoff Time ”): (i) all Term Loans, including all Initial Term Loans, and all accrued interest, fees and other Obligations in respect thereof (other than contingent obligations that by their terms survive repayment) shall have been paid and satisfied in full; (ii) all Term Commitments, including all Initial Term Commitments, shall have terminated, and the Total Term Commitments and the Total Term Loan Exposures shall each be zero; (iii) no Term Lender shall have any further obligation to make any Term Loan, and no Term Loan, Term Commitment or Term Loan Exposure shall remain outstanding; (iv) any Note evidencing a Term Loan shall be deemed cancelled, and each Lender holding any such Note shall return it marked “cancelled” upon request; and Page 2 (v) no amount shall be payable under Section 2.11 of the Credit Agreement in respect of such repayment to any Lender party to this Second Amendment, and any Lender party to this Second Amendment, solely on its own behalf, hereby waives any such amount. (c) Waiver of Notice . The Administrative Agent and each Lender party hereto waives any notice of prepayment required under Section 5.1 of the Credit Agreement in respect of the repayment contemplated by this Section 2.3, and any such notice shall be deemed timely given. (d) Reliance . The Administrative Agent acknowledges that the Second Lien Administrative Agent and the Second Lien Lenders are relying on this Section 2.3 in entering into the Second Lien Credit Agreement and are express third-party beneficiaries of this Section 2.3 entitled to rely on it. (e) Revolving Facility Unaffected . Nothing in this Section 2.3 shall release, reduce or impair the Revolving Commitments, the Revolving Loans, the Letters of Credit, the Guarantee or any Lien under the Security Documents, each of which shall remain in full force and effect, and the Guarantee and such Lien shall continue to secure all Obligations that remain outstanding. Section 3. Conditions Precedent to Effectiveness . This Second Amendment shall become effective subject to the satisfaction of each of the following conditions precedent (or waiver thereof in accordance with Section 13.1 of the Credit Agreement) (the date on which each of the following conditions is so satisfied or waived, the “ Second Amendment Effective Date ”): 3.1 Second Amendment . The Administrative Agent (or its counsel) shall have received from the Borrower, the other Credit Parties, and Lenders constituting at least the Majority Lenders, counterparts (in such number as may be requested by the Administrative Agent) of this Second Amendment signed on behalf of such Persons. 3.2 Second Lien Credit Documents . The Administrative Agent (or its counsel) shall have received true and correct fully executed copies of the Second Lien Credit Agreement and any other principal Second Lien Credit Documents dated as of the Second Amendment Effective Date reasonably requested by the Administrative Agent. 3.3 Intercreditor Agreement . The Administrative Agent (or its counsel) shall have received from each party thereto duly executed counterparts (in such number as may be requested by the Administrative Agent) of the Second Lien Intercreditor Agreement. 3.4 Fees and Expenses . The Administrative Agent shall have received all (a) fees due and payable on or prior to the Second Amendment Effective Date and (b) other expenses and amounts required to be reimbursed or paid by the Borrower hereunder or under any other Credit Document for which invoices have been provided to the Borrower at least two (2) Business Days prior to the Second Amendment Effective Date. 3.5 Mortgages . The Collateral Agent shall have received fully executed and notarized Mortgages for recording in all appropriate places in all applicable jurisdictions, encumbering such Oil and Gas Properties as may be necessary so that (a) the Collateral Coverage Minimum (determined after giving effect to the incurrence of the Second Lien Term Loans) is met and (b) the Oil and Gas Properties encumbered by mortgages securing the Second Lien Term Loans and those encumbered by Mortgages securing the Obligations are identical. Page 3 3.6 Term Loan Repayment . The Administrative Agent shall have received evidence that the Term Loan Payoff Amount has been or, substantially concurrently with the Second Amendment Effective Date, will be paid in full in cash from the proceeds of the Second Lien Term Loans, Revolving Loans and cash on hand. Section 4. Miscellaneous . 4.1 Confirmation . The provisions of the Credit Agreement, as amended by this Second Amendment, shall remain in full force and effect following the Second Amendment Effective Date. 4.2 Ratification and Affirmation; Representations and Warranties . Each Credit Party hereby: (a) acknowledges the terms of this Second Amendment; (b) ratifies and affirms its obligations under, and acknowledges its continued liability under, each Credit Document to which it is a party and agrees that each such Credit Document remains in full force and effect as expressly amended hereby; (c) agrees that from and after the Second Amendment Effective Date, each reference to the Credit Agreement in the other Credit Documents shall be deemed to be a reference to the Credit Agreement, as amended by this Second Amendment; and (d) represents and warrants to the Lenders that as of the date hereof, after giving effect to the terms of this Second Amendment: (i) the representations and warranties set forth in each Credit Document to which it is a party are true and correct in all material respects (except that such materiality qualifier shall not be applicable to any representation or warranty that already is qualified or modified by materiality in the text thereof) except to the extent any such representations and warranties are expressly limited to an earlier date, in which case, such representations and warranties shall continue to be true and correct as of such specified earlier date and (ii) no Default, Event of Default or Borrowing Base Deficiency has occurred and is continuing. The execution, delivery and effectiveness of this Second Amendment shall not, except as expressly provided herein, operate as a waiver of any right, power or remedy of any Lender or the Administrative Agent under any of the Credit Documents. 4.3 Counterparts . This Second Amendment may be executed by one or more of the parties to this Second Amendment on any number of separate counterparts (including by facsimile or other electronic transmission, i.e., a “pdf” or a “tif”), and all of said counterparts taken together shall be deemed to constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page of this Second Amendment by fax, as an attachment to an email or other similar electronic means shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart of this Second Amendment. 4.4 Integration . This Second Amendment and the other Credit Documents represent the agreement of the Borrower, the Guarantors, the Collateral Agent, the Administrative Agent and the Lenders with respect to the subject matter hereof and thereof, and there are no promises, undertakings, representations or warranties by the Borrower, the Guarantors, any Agent or any Lender relative to the subject matter hereof not expressly set forth or referred to herein or in the other Credit Documents. Page 4 4.5 GOVERNING LAW . THIS SECOND AMENDMENT SHALL BE GOVERNED BY, AND CONSTRUED AND INTERPRETED IN ACCORDANCE WITH, THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK. 4.6 Payment of Expenses . In accordance with Section 13.5 of the Credit Agreement, the Borrower agrees to pay or reimburse the Administrative Agent for all of its reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred in connection with this Second Amendment, any other documents prepared in connection herewith and the transactions contemplated hereby, including, without limitation, the reasonable fees, charges and disbursements of counsel to the Administrative Agent. 4.7 Severability . Any provision of this Second Amendment that is prohibited or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall, as to such jurisdiction, be ineffective to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without invalidating the remaining provisions hereof, and any such prohibition or unenforceability in any jurisdiction shall not invalidate or render unenforceable such provision in any other jurisdiction. 4.8 Successors and Assigns . This Second Amendment shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns. 4.9 Credit Document . This Second Amendment is a “Credit Document” as defined and described in the Credit Agreement, and all of the terms and provisions of the Credit Agreement relating to Credit Documents shall apply hereto. 4.10 Interpretation . On and after the Second Amendment Effective Date, each reference in the Credit Agreement to “this Agreement,” “hereunder,” “hereof” or words of like import referring to the Credit Agreement shall mean and be a reference to the Credit Agreement, as amended by this Second Amendment. 4.11 Second Lien Intercreditor Agreement . Each Lender party hereto (constituting at least the Majority Lenders) hereby authorizes and directs the Administrative Agent and the Collateral Agent to execute and deliver the Second Lien Intercreditor Agreement. 4.12 Consent and Waiver Regarding Deposit Account Control Agreements . The Administrative Agent, the Collateral Agent and the Lenders party hereto hereby (a) acknowledge and agree that Liens on the Controlled Accounts securing the Second Lien Obligations (the “ Junior Deposit Account Liens ”) are subject to the Second Lien Intercreditor Agreement and permitted under Section 10.2(bb) of the Credit Agreement (as amended hereby) and (b) solely to the extent required under any Deposit Account Control Agreement and solely for the purposes of any such Deposit Account Control Agreement, consent to the existence of Junior Deposit Account Liens so long as such Junior Deposit Account Liens are subject to the Second Lien Intercreditor Agreement and so long as they do not secure Second Lien Obligations in an aggregate principal amount in excess of $385,000,000 (such cap not to include accrued or capitalized interest, premiums, fees, expenses and original issue discount). text: EX-10.1 2 merlininc8-kxexhibit101.htm EX-10.1 Document Exhibit 10.1 TRANSITION AGREEMENT This Transition Agreement (“ Agreement ”) is entered into by and between Merlin, Inc., a Delaware corporation (along with any successor thereto, the “ Company ”), and Matthew George (“ Executive ”). The Company and Executive are referred to herein collectively as the “ Parties .” WHEREAS , Executive has been employed by the Company and has served as its Chief Executive Officer and the Chairman of the Board of Directors (the “ Board ”) of the Company; WHEREAS , the Parties have agreed that Executive will transition to the role of Founder and Advisor effective as of November 18, 2026 (the “ Transition Date ”); WHEREAS , Executive is eligible to participate in the Merlin, Inc. Executive Severance Plan (the “ Severance Plan ”) at the Tier I participation level; WHEREAS , as of the date hereof, Executive has stock options (the “ Options ”) outstanding under the Merlin, Inc. 2018 Equity Incentive Plan (as Amended and Restated on March 16, 2026) (the “ 2018 Equity Incentive Plan ”) and time-based restricted stock units (the “ RSU Awards ”) outstanding under the Merlin, Inc. 2026 Incentive Award Plan (the “ 2026 Equity Incentive Plan ” and, together with the 2018 Equity Incentive Plan, the “ Equity Incentive Plans ”); WHEREAS , the Parties desire to set forth the Executive’s separation benefits and obligations, the terms of Executive’s service to the Company as an independent consultant following the Transition Date, and to finally, fully and completely resolve all matters arising from or during Executive’s employment; and NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the mutual promises and mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Transition to Founder and Advisor; Advisory Period . (a) Effective as of the Transition Date, Executive shall cease to serve as the Chief Executive Officer of the Company and Chairman of the Board, and Executive shall resign from all of Executive’s positions with the Company and its affiliates, including all director, officer, employee and fiduciary positions (including as trustee), as applicable, except for Executive’s move forward position as Founder and Advisor, as described in this Section 1 . Executive shall execute all documents and take such further steps as may be reasonably required to effectuate such terminations. As of the Transition Date, Executive shall not make any representations, execute any documents or take any other actions on behalf of the Company, except as requested by the Board consistent with his duties as Founder and Advisor. (b) In consideration for the treatment of Executive’s equity awards as set forth in Section 2(d) , Executive shall provide advice and services to the Company as an independent consultant in the role of Founder and Advisor from and including the Transition Date until the first anniversary of the Transition Date, unless earlier terminated by Executive for any reason or by the Company for Cause (as defined below) (the date of such termination, the “ Advisory Termination Date ” and the period from the Transition Date until the Advisory Termination Date, the “ Advisory Period ”). As Founder and Advisor, Executive will report to the Board, with responsibility for providing advice to the Board, when and as reasonably requested by the Board and agreed by Executive, at mutually agreed times and not to exceed 15 hours per month (except as otherwise mutually agreed). In addition, during the Advisory Period, Executive agrees to cooperate and provide reasonable assistance, at the reasonable request of the Company and at mutually agreed times, in the orderly transitioning of Executive’s duties and responsibilities to such other persons as the Company shall designate. For purposes of this Agreement, “ Cause ” means: (i) Executive’s willful or material unauthorized use or disclosure of confidential information or trade secrets of the Company or any of its subsidiaries (except where Executive is exercising Executive’s his requested duties to the Company or protected rights under Section 5(b) , or as otherwise required by applicable law) or any material breach of a written agreement between Executive and the Company or any of its subsidiaries, including without limitation, this Agreement, in each case, that could reasonably be expected to result in economic or reputational harm to the Company or its subsidiaries; (ii) Executive’s conviction of or the entry of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere by Executive to, a felony under the laws of the United States or any state thereof or any crime involving dishonesty or moral turpitude (or any similar crime in any jurisdiction outside the United States); (iii) Executive’s willful and material failure or refusal to substantially perform Executive’s duties as Founder and Advisor in a manner consistent with such duties as contemplated hereunder; (iv) Any act of fraud, embezzlement or material misappropriation committed by Executive against the Company or any of its subsidiaries; or (v) Any dishonesty, acts, omissions, or statements by Executive which could reasonably be expected to result in material economic or reputational harm to the Company or its subsidiaries. Provided, however that in the case of clauses (i), (iii) and (v), if capable of cure, the Company shall have given Executive written notice thereof and Executive shall have not cured such event within thirty (30) days. No act or omission shall be “willful” unless taken or omitted to be taken without good faith belief that such act or omission was for the benefit of the Company or if such act or omission was based on advice of counsel.
